refactor: remove condenseOldToolResults (prefix-cache killer)

condenseOldToolResults was a proxy-layer mechanical condenser (stub large old
tool results to a 400-char head) introduced in v0.1.0. It runs EVERY turn and
rewrites stable history (full→stub as a sliding window moves), which breaks
provider prefix caching for everything after the shifted message.

With ACP's model-driven compress tool now handling context management, condense
is both redundant and harmful (the two are fundamentally opposed: condense
mutates stable history each turn; prefix caching requires byte-stable history).

Removed across 8 source files + 7 test files:
- anthropic.ts: condenseOldToolResults, CondenseOptions, CondenseResult,
  CONDENSED_TAG
- openai.ts / responses.ts: import + re-export
- server.ts: applyCondense fn, 3 call sites (→ turn.messages), stats field
- config.ts: condense ProxyOptions/FileConfig block + 4 ACP_* env parses
- session.ts: condensedToolResults field
- persist.ts: field (deserialize still loads old files — extra field ignored)
- cli.ts / README.md: references

Tests: 145 → 139 (removed 6 condense-specific tests across 2 files).

fix: isTitleGen no longer flips system prompt between turn 1 and 2+ (cache fix)

The OpenAI/chat path keyed isTitleGen on BOTH (maxTokens<=200) AND
(messages.length<=2). The second condition meant turn 1 of ANY conversation
(max_tokens=8192, 2 messages) had shouldInject=false → no compress prompt in
system, no compress tool. Turn 2+ → shouldInject=true → system bytes change.

This rewrite of the system block between turn 1 and turn 2+ breaks the provider
prefix cache for everything after the system prompt (i.e. the entire
conversation) on every conversation.

Fix: key isTitleGen ONLY on maxTokens<=200 (a real title-gen signal). Message
count was a false proxy for 'this is a throwaway request'. The Anthropic and
Responses paths never had this bug (they always inject, so their system is
stable from turn 1).
fix: preserve Anthropic cache_control through core round-trip + system block

fix: route auto-update logs through the tee logger (file + stderr)

Previously checkForUpdate only emitted to stderr via console.error, and only
on the success/failure path — the file log showed nothing about update
activity, and the periodic check was a silent black box. Now the full cycle
is observable in the log:
- startup: 'auto-update enabled (checking every 180s)'
- throttle skip: 'check skipped (throttled, Ns until next)'
- registry fetch: 'checking npm registry for billion-context…'
- no update: 'current=0.1.6 latest=0.1.6 (up to date)'
- new version: 'new version found: 0.1.6 → 0.1.7, installing…'
- installed: 'installed 0.1.6 → 0.1.7. Restart to finish.'
- already-notified: 'latest=0.1.7 already installed this run, awaiting restart'
- failures: registry error / install failure with reason

All go through logger.log() so they land in the file too, matching the
rest of the proxy's observability story.

release v0.1.7

fix: cross-platform robustness (port crash, Windows shutdown, persist, BOM, /tmp)

C1 (all platforms): server.listen() had no 'error' listener, so EADDRINUSE
(port taken) / EACCES (privileged port) threw an unhandled 'error' event and
aborted the process before graceful-shutdown could flush sessions. User hit
this as 'bili start --port 44445' crashing with a Node.js stack. Now caught,
logged with a human hint ('port N is already in use'), sessions flushed, and
exit(1).

M1 (Windows): SIGTERM is never delivered on Windows (Node can listen but the
kernel won't raise it), so taskkill / service managers / NSSM stopped the
proxy without triggering flushAllSessions — losing up to debounce-ms of
session state. Add SIGBREAK handler (raised by Ctrl+Break and most Windows
process terminators) to the same graceful-shutdown path.

M2 (Windows): persist.ts writeNow did writeFile+rename without a try/catch.
On Windows, fs.rename (MoveFileEx) throws EPERM/EBUSY when the destination
is held open by AV scan / search indexer / concurrent flushSync / SMB share.
The throw propagated, left an orphan .tmp-* file, and lost the write. Wrap
it: on failure, unlink the .tmp file and surface the error.

m1 (Windows): server.ts debug dump hardcoded '/tmp/...'. Windows has no
/tmp, so debug dumps silently failed (ENOENT swallowed by try/catch). Use
os.tmpdir().

m2 (all platforms): config.ts safeReadJson did not strip a UTF-8 BOM. Windows
Notepad saves UTF-8 'with BOM'; JSON.parse('\uFEFF...') throws SyntaxError,
silently dropping the whole config file. Strip leading BOM before parse.

m4 (all platforms): no global uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers.
Background work (compress loops, auto-update, initSessions) escaping the
per-request try/catch would abort the process (Node 20+ default). Add
top-level handlers that log loudly instead of crashing.

fix: remaining cross-platform + robustness (logger rotation, SSE drain, host docs)

m3 (all platforms): logger only checked size at startup; a long-running proxy's
log grew without bound. Track bytesWritten and rotate at runtime when the

closes the connection.

container (0.0.0.0) cases with a security warning, in both README.md and

release v0.1.9

fix: make update throttle logs unambiguous

The old line 'check skipped (throttled, Ns until next)' only showed the
countdown, which looked wrong when it grew between consecutive skips (a real
check had reset the timestamp in between, but we only logged the skips).

Now log both axes explicitly:
  'throttled — last checked 42s ago, retry in 138s'
and the real-check line records when the last check happened:
  'checking npm registry … (last check 180s ago)'

Monotonic 'last checked Ns ago' can't look backwards; 'retry in Ms' is the
true countdown.

feat: first check per process ignores throttle (startup check)

A freshly started proxy was inheriting a stale throttle timestamp from the
previous run, delaying the first real update check by up to the full interval
(180s). The user saw only 'check skipped (throttled)' lines for minutes on
startup, making auto-update look broken.

Now the first checkForUpdate() in each process always runs a real registry
fetch (marked '(startup check)' in the log); subsequent calls honor the
shared cross-process throttle. The 'first check done' marker lives in the
existing notified Set (as a sentinel key), so it resets on restart — which
is exactly when a bumped version takes effect anyway.

Verified: with a stale throttle file (1h old), startup → 10s later →
'checking npm registry for billion-context (startup check)…' immediately,
no throttle skip.

fix: retry auto-update on transient install failure (Bug A)

The notified.add(latest) was executed unconditionally, before checking
whether installLatest() actually succeeded.  A single transient failure
(network hiccup, EACCES, registry 5xx) caused the version to be marked
as 'notified' anyway.  Every subsequent 3-min cycle then hit the
'already installed this run' guard and skipped — so one transient error
permanently disabled auto-update for the entire process lifetime.

Fix: move notified.add(latest) inside the success branch.  On failure,
do not add to notified so the next throttle cycle retries naturally.

Also fix stale comment in cli.ts:164 ('6h throttle' → 'the throttle';
CHECK_INTERVAL_MS is 3 min, not 6h) and bump version 0.1.10 → 0.1.11.

ci: enforce version-only-on-release-branches (AGENTS.md §4 + guard)

Adds two layers of protection so the 'version' field can never be casually
bumped:

1. AGENTS.md §4 — new 'Version Bumps' subsection (sibling to the npm Publish
   prohibition): two hard rules — version changes ONLY on *_release-v*
   branches, and a release commit changes ONLY version. Includes the reason
   (CI trigger detection + merge-conflict avoidance) and a canned reply for
   when a human asks to bundle a version bump into content.

2. ci.yml — new 'version-guard' job that runs on every PR: if the branch is
   NOT *_release-v* and the diff touches the '"version"' line in
   package.json, the job fails with a ::error annotation. Release branches
   skip the check.

This prevents the exact failure that hit PR#32 (version bundled into a
non-release context → three-way merge conflict + broken CI trigger).

docs(agents): no-op release required before shipping changes to auto-update

The auto-update code (src/update.ts) is load-bearing for every future
upgrade. A broken release bricks the upgrade path for anyone who hits
it — they can never auto-update again. This documents the safety rule:
any change to update.ts MUST be preceded by a no-op release that
validates the existing upgrade path is healthy end-to-end, using the
old (trusted) code, before the new code ships.

Includes the v0.1.22 concrete example (Windows fix staged in PR#44,
no-op validation release in PR#46 first).

fix(windows): cross-platform auto-update — no shell-out to tar/cp binaries

Windows has no `tar` or `cp` in PATH by default, so auto-update
(extract npm tarball + copy over install dir) failed silently on
Windows, leaving users stuck on their installed version forever.

Replaced both external commands with cross-platform Node APIs:
- tar extraction: `tar` npm package (pure JS, same lib npm CLI uses)
  via `tar.x({ file, cwd, strip: 1 })` — replaces `execFile("tar", ...)`
- dir copy: Node built-in `fs/promises` `cp()` with recursive+force —
  replaces `execFile("cp", ...)`

`tar` is a build-time dep (devDependencies) — tsup bundles it into
dist at build time, so the runtime footprint (what users install) is
unchanged: still only acp-kernel as a runtime dependency.

Verified: real npm tarball extracts correctly (package.json version
matches), and fs.cp merges contents into target dir without clobbering
existing files (equivalent to `cp -r src/. dst/`).

feat: hot-reload routes via web UI 'Apply' button — no restart needed

The web UI's Save wrote the config file but required a manual bili
restart to take effect. Users (especially on Windows, running bili
without an interactive terminal) hit this: they'd save config in the
browser, keep using the proxy, and all requests still went to the old
upstream because the running process never re-read the file.

## Changes
- config.ts: export loadRoutes() — re-reads routes from the config
  file (same precedence as loadOptions: ACP_PROVIDERS path > inline
  providers). Returns a fresh ProviderRoutes.
- server.ts: POST /__acp/config/reload — calls loadRoutes(), then
  clears+refills opts.routes IN PLACE so all in-flight handle()
  closures (which captured opts by ref) see the new routes. Only
  routes reload — port/host/upstream can't change on a running server.
- web.ts: 'Apply' button next to 'Save'. Save writes the file (as
  before); Apply hot-loads routes into the running process. Apply is
  blocked if there are unsaved edits (prompts 'Save your changes first').

## UX
- Save → 'Saved N providers — click Apply to activate'
- Apply → 'Applied — N providers active (no restart needed)'
- Dirty notice: 'click Save then click Apply to activate without restart'

Verified: PUT writes config, POST reload updates in-memory routes
immediately, subsequent request routes to the new upstream without restart.

## Zero-config routing (Issue #50)

Users no longer need a config file to route. Prefixing the client's
baseURL with the proxy origin + /p/ embeds the full upstream URL in
the path:

    client baseURL:  http://127.0.0.1:8787/p/https://api.openai.com/v1

resolveUpstream detects /p/http(s):// at the path start, strips the
prefix, and uses the embedded URL verbatim as the upstream. Returns
provider="p" so stats/labels can tell zero-config requests apart.

The /p/ prefix keeps zero-config requests physically separate from
control endpoints (/__acp/*) and named-config routes (/<name>/*) —
no collision possible.

Three modes now coexist:
- /p/https://...  → zero-config (new)
- /zhipu/...      → named provider (existing, unchanged)
- /__acp/...      → control endpoints (existing)

## Auto-fetch context from models.dev (Issue #55)

models.dev/models.json is a 254KB registry (301 providers, every model
with limit.context) that opencode itself uses as its model registry.
We fetch + cache it (24h TTL, disk cache for offline) as the context-
window source for zero-config routes that have no per-model config.

src/registry.ts: loadRegistry() (fetch + disk cache + TTL), contextFromRegistry(model, host).
  - providerFromHost maps known hosts → provider ids
    (api.openai.com→openai, open.bigmodel.cn→zhipuai, etc.)
  - lookup tries 'provider/model' then bare 'model'
Fallback chain: per-model config → registry (zero-config only) → prefix table → default.

Registry is preloaded in the background at startup (non-blocking).
Misses fall back gracefully; offline-first via disk cache.

feat: MITM transparent proxy for OAuth/subscription clients (ZCode)

Clients that lock the model endpoint behind an OAuth/subscription login
(ZCode coding plan, Codex ChatGPT account, Claude Code subscription) cannot
use the existing /bili/<url> path-routing mode — their auth is bound to a
non-standard endpoint they won't let you reconfigure. MITM mode lets them
route through the proxy transparently: the client sets httpProxy (an HTTP
CONNECT proxy) + trusts our root CA; we TLS-terminate whitelisted model
hosts, inject compression into the plaintext, then forward to the real
upstream with the client's Authorization header (OAuth token) preserved
verbatim, so subscription billing/discounts stay intact.

Architecture: CONNECT handler TLS-terminates with a node-forge-signed host
cert and feeds the decrypted socket back into the same http server via
emit('connection', tlsSocket) — the existing handle()/forward() pipeline
runs unchanged, with a socket marker telling resolveUpstream() the real
upstream origin. Non-whitelisted hosts are blind-tunnelled (never decrypted).
node-forge is a devDependency bundled inline by tsup — dist stays zero
runtime deps.

fix(build): inject createRequire banner for node-forge CJS-in-ESM

node-forge is a CommonJS module that calls require('crypto'). When
tsup/esbuild inlines it into our ESM output, the __require shim throws
'Dynamic require of crypto is not supported' because require is undefined
in an ESM context. Inject a createRequire-based require at the top of the
bundle so the shim can load node built-ins. Verified: bili start --debug
now boots and prints the MITM banner.

fix: inject all 4 ACP tools on Anthropic path (was only compress)

The system prompt (buildCompressSystemPrompt) tells the model it has five
context-management tools (compress/decompress/search_context/acp_status) and
documents how to call each. But the Anthropic request path only injected
COMPRESS_TOOL as a function tool, so clients on that path (ZCode, Claude
Code) saw the tool docs in the system prompt but could not actually call
decompress/search_context/acp_status — the model reported 'I can see them
described but they are not in my tool list'.

Add Anthropic-format definitions (name + description + input_schema) for the
other three tools and inject all four on the Anthropic path, matching what
the OpenAI and Responses paths already do. Fixes the mismatch surfaced by
the ZCode MITM test (prompt injected fine, tools did not).

feat(anthropic): intercept & exec all 4 ACP tools in stream

stream.ts only intercepted COMPRESS_TOOL_NAME; decompress/search_context/
acp_status tool_use blocks passed through to the client → 'Tool not found'.

Mirror the OpenAI path: block all 4 PROXY_TOOL_NAMES tools, execute them
internally (executeAnthropicProxyTool, same logic as compress-loop.ts
executeProxyTool), emit the result as a text delta replacing the tool_use.

BlockState: isCompress→toolName:string|null. Non-streaming rewriteJsonResponse
updated the same way.

fix(anthropic): preserve upstream usage in synthetic message_delta

When a proxy tool_use was converted to text (compress/decompress/
search_context/acp_status), the upstream message_delta was suppressed but
its usage discarded, and the synthetic replacement hardcoded usage:{}.
ZCode's Zod schema requires usage.output_tokens:number → 'Turn execution
failed'.

Capture upstream usage on both converted/non-converted paths; pass it to
buildStopReasonRewrite. Default output_tokens:0 so strict clients still
pass even if upstream omitted it.

feat: Anthropic multi-round compress loop (tool results reach upstream)

The Anthropic path used rewriteSseStream — a single-pass rewriter that
intercepted proxy tool_use blocks and emitted their result as a text delta
TO THE CLIENT. That result never went back to the upstream LLM, so
query-type tools (acp_status, search_context) broke the model's reasoning
chain: the model called acp_status, proxy ran it, but the model never saw
the result → couldn't decide to compress next → client hung.

New compressLoopAnthropicStream mirrors compress-loop.ts (OpenAI chat) and
compress-loop-responses.ts: intercept proxy tool_use → execute → push
assistant(tool_use) + user(tool_result) back into the request → re-request
upstream → loop until the model stops calling proxy tools. The tool RESULT
reaches the model, so acp_status→compress flows work.

- New: src/compress-loop-anthropic.ts (multi-round SSE loop)
- server.ts: anthropic streaming branch now uses the loop (same pattern as
  openai/responses branches) instead of rewriteSseStream
- Index remapping: proxy tool_use blocks suppressed, client sees sequential
  indices continuing across rounds; round 2+ content gets remapped indices
- message_start forwarded in round 1 only; message_delta/message_stop always
  suppressed and re-emitted with accumulated output_tokens at the end

fix: prefer client conversation header to avoid session collisions

conversationSignalAnthropic/Openai/Responses were called with only
opts.sessionHeader (a user-configured header name, usually unset), so the
conversation dimension fell through to the content fingerprint fallback —
hash of the first user message's first 200 chars. IDE clients like ZCode
inject a fixed <system-reminder> (workspace context) at the start of every
new conversation, so different conversations collided on the same 200-char
prefix → same sessionId → compression state (blocks) leaked across
sessions.

clientConversationHeader() already extracts the strongest signal
(x-session-id / x-session-affinity / x-acp-session / x-opencode-session),
but it was only used for the web-UI label, not for the session-id
derivation. Now the client header is preferred for session-id too;
content fingerprint remains the last-resort fallback for clients that
send no conversation header at all (pi).

fix: 5 bugs from GLM bug-audit (crash/leak/nan/substring/multi-tool)

Bug 1 (server.ts): cacheHitPct NaN when inputTokens=0 (divide-by-zero
  on GLM which reports input_tokens=0 in message_start). Guard now

Bug 2 (server.ts): non-streaming arrayBuffer() throw skipped

Bug 3 (mitm.ts): MITM TLSSocket had no 'error' listener — a TLS
  handshake error (client cert reject / abrupt disconnect) crashed the

  boundary — 'api.openai.com' matched key 'penai.com'. Now requires
  exact host match or '.subdomain' boundary.

  A chunk carrying 2+ tool calls dropped the args of the 2nd+. Now
  loops over all entries, accumulating compress args + marking sawReal

fix: proxy stripped input_tokens from synthetic message_delta (ZCode context display)

Root cause: compress-loop-anthropic emits a synthetic message_delta at the
end of the stream to close the response. It only carried output_tokens.
But GLM (and many providers) put the REAL input_tokens + cache_read in
message_delta — which the proxy SUPPRESSES. So standard clients (ZCode)
reading message_delta saw input=0 and reported a tiny context size
(e.g. 2166 for a 300k-token review).

Direct GLM→ZCode works fine; the proxy was the regression (introduced
when compress-loop-anthropic replaced the single-pass rewriter).

Fix: accumulate input_tokens + cache_read across rounds (alongside the
existing output_tokens accumulation) and include all three in the
synthetic message_delta usage. Not ZCode-specific — any Anthropic-spec
client that reads usage from message_delta now gets correct values.

fix: system prompt not counted in contextTokens — nudge never fired for IDE clients

Root cause: contextTokens was computed from anthropicToCore()/responsesToCore()
output, but BOTH exclude the system prompt:
  - Anthropic: body.system (huge for ZCode — workspace reminders) is collected
    by extractSystem() but never added to msgs, so estimateTokensFast missed it.
  - Responses: body.instructions (huge for Codex) + system/developer items are
    collected into systemParts but never added to msgs.
  - OpenAI: system is message[0] → already in msgs → already correct.

Effect: ZCode review session showed contextTokens=38584 while real input was
1.7M tokens. The undercount meant usage stayed at ~4% of 1M limit → nudge
threshold never crossed → compression never triggered, even at 1.7M tokens.

Fix: concatenate the system text into the tokenCount estimate for the
Anthropic and Responses paths. OpenAI path unchanged (already correct).

fix: tokenCount uses real upstream input_tokens, never estimates

Root cause: tokenCount (drives the nudge/compress decision) was computed via
estimateTokensFast = chars/4. This undercounts CJK text 3-4x (Chinese chars
count as 0.25 token instead of ~1), so Chinese-heavy sessions (ZCode reviewing
a CN project: real 50k tokens) read as ~35k — never reaching the 50k compress
threshold. Compression never fired.

The upstream API already reports the authoritative input_tokens in every
usage (Anthropic message_delta, OpenAI prompt_tokens, Responses input_tokens).
That is the ground truth — no estimate (neither chars/4 nor a BPE tokenizer)
can beat it. Use it.

Changes:
- session.stats: add lastInputTokens (single-turn, overwritten each turn).
  Existing cumulative inputTokens is kept for the web UI totals.
- compress-loop-{anthropic,openai,responses}.ts onCacheUsage/usage: also
  set lastInputTokens = input (overwrite, not accumulate).
- server.ts three prepare* branches: tokenCount = session.stats.lastInputTokens.

  calls removed from the tokenCount path.
- persist.ts: round-trip lastInputTokens with backward-compat (old files
  default to 0).
- tests: stats literals updated.

estimateTokensFast is still imported (used by buildStatusReport for the
acp_status display breakdown), but no longer drives any compress/nudge decision.

fix: logger silently lost all output when bili.log was deleted/replaced mid-run

Root cause: createWriteStream opens the inode at startup and holds it. If the
path is later deleted/replaced (rebuild, restart, rm, logrotate), the stream
keeps writing to the now-unlinked inode — writes 'succeed' but vanish into a
black hole. The proxy appears to run but produces no log file, even though
diagNudge/forward logs fire normally.

Observed: PID 2359696's fd 22 -> bili.log.old (deleted); fresh bili.log was
0 bytes for the whole session, so nudge/growth diagnostics never surfaced.

Fix: check existsSync(logPath) before each write; reopen if the file has
vanished. Cheap stat per log line; only reopens on the rare delete case.

fix: non-streaming usage not captured + OpenAI streaming include_usage not injected

Two more gaps in the same class as commit 45aae16 (tokenCount must be the
real upstream input_tokens, never an estimate):

1. Non-streaming path (server.ts rewrite*JsonResponse branch) never read
   json.usage → lastInputTokens stayed 0 → compression/truncate never
   fired for non-streaming sessions. Now extracts input_tokens/prompt_tokens
   (per-protocol field names) + cache + output and writes to session stats,
   aligned with the streaming loops' onCacheUsage.

2. OpenAI Chat Completions streaming only sends usage in the final chunk
   when stream_options.include_usage=true. The proxy never injected it,
   so streaming OpenAI sessions whose client didn't set it also got
   lastInputTokens=0. Now forced on for any streaming OpenAI request that
   doesn't already opt in. Anthropic/Responses emit usage unconditionally,
   so this is OpenAI-specific.

Found by researcher audit (del_mslfy6j8_shi9). Task two (self-built vs
kernel) all clear — no duplicates, kernel text constants correctly reused.

fix: tokenCount used only new input_tokens, ignored cached tokens (cached sessions never compressed)

Critical: lastInputTokens = input_tokens only, ignoring cache_read_input_tokens.
Providers split the prompt into new (input_tokens) + cached (cache_read_input_tokens).
The TOTAL context that fills the window is the SUM. Using only input_tokens makes
a cached session look tiny — e.g. ZCode review showed usage=0% (601/1M) while the
real context was ~40k (601 new + ~40k cached system prompt). With cache_read
ignored, the nudge never fired and compression never happened even though the
context was genuinely large.

Fixed all 4 usage-capture sites (3 streaming loops + non-streaming path):
  lastInputTokens = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens  (total context)
  inputTokens stat (for cost display) still accumulates only new input_tokens.

Also committed earlier this turn (86ce78f): non-streaming usage capture +
OpenAI stream_options.include_usage injection — both from researcher audit.

fix: logger stderr.write EPIPE crashed the proxy (uncaughtException)

Root cause of the vanishing-proxy + empty-bili.log mystery. log() called
process.stderr.write(line) WITHOUT try/catch. When the stderr reader closes
(terminal shut, piped process exited, broken pipe) write() throws EPIPE.
As an uncaught exception in a hot path, it killed the whole proxy — which is
why every bili start --debug session silently died and bili.log stayed 0 bytes
(the process never lived long enough to write much, and the file inode was
already detached).

Fixed: wrap BOTH stderr.write and the file-write block in try/catch so
logging can never crash the server. Combined with the earlier existsSync()
reopen, the log file is now reliable.

subsection under Quickstart Option A. ZCode is the one client that cannot
use the /bili/ prefix (its OAuth provider hardcodes the endpoint), so it
needs the MITM transparent-proxy path: set HTTP proxy + CA cert path in

logger.ts: rewrite to be crash-proof and self-healing:
- process.stderr.write wrapped in try/catch (EPIPE from a closed reader
  used to throw an uncaughtException and kill the whole proxy — the real
  reason bili.log was always empty).
- the held WriteStream now listens for 'error' and drops itself so the
  next write reopens; stream.writable checked before write. Recovers from

fix: compress found 0 chars — ctx.messages used processedMessages (folded) not originals

Root cause: the compress/decompress/acp_status loops received
prepared.processedMessages as their ctx.messages. But processedMessages is
processTurn's OUTPUT, where messages already covered by a compression block
have their text replaced with placeholders/summaries. When the model later
called compress with refs pointing into those messages, collectBlockContent
found empty text → 'Total compressible content too small (0 chars)' and the
tool failed.

This only manifests AFTER the first successful compression in a session (round
1 has no blocks yet → processedMessages still has full text → works). From
round 2 on, every compress call into a folded region failed.

Fix: capture the raw CoreMessages from the protocol conversion (anthropicToCore/
openaiToCore/responsesToCore output, BEFORE processTurn) as prepared.originalMessages
and feed THOSE to all three loops. processTurn preserves message ids, so the
refs the model sees are identical — but originalMessages still carries the full
text for collectBlockContent to read.

Matches pai-acp's pattern (entriesToCoreMessages from raw session entries, not
processTurn output).

fix(#5): per-session write serialization + rename EPERM/EBUSY retry (Windows)

Root cause: writeNow/flushSync were not serialized per-session — two
concurrent writes to the same session (debounce timer firing while a previous
write is in flight, or flushSync during eviction) both call fs.rename on the
same destination. On Linux rename is atomic; on Windows (MoveFileEx with
MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) it throws EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES when the destination
is momentarily held (AV scan, search indexer, SMB share).

Fix:

prepareCountTokens mirrors exactly what the next /v1/messages would forward

fix: route Responses reasoning through compression pipeline

Responses API `reasoning` items were treated as opaque preamble and
re-sent verbatim every turn, accumulating without bound (broke Codex's
prompt-cache prefix and blew up context). Anthropic `thinking` already
flowed through the compression pipeline as a tracked message and was
bounded; only the Responses path was broken.

Route `reasoning` the same way: convert each item to a tracked
BiliMessage (contentType "reasoning") that carries the original item
verbatim in rawResponsesItem. The kernel hides the message once its
range is compressed, so old reasoning drops automatically and never
needs to be merged into a text summary (which would corrupt the opaque
encrypted_content).

finish_reason='tool_calls' and NO tool_calls in the body — causing the
client (pi/opencode) to hang indefinitely waiting for tool calls that

the proxy result back to the model so it can continue, matching baseline

fix(responses): preserve systemParts + preamble in V2 loop re-request

Round-2 buildRequest for the Responses (Codex) protocol rebuilt the upstream input via coreToResponses(coreMessages) with only the compress prompt as the developer message. This dropped two things round-1 preserved via the projection:

1. systemParts (the original 'instructions') — round-1 put [...systemParts, prompt] in the developer message; round-2 sent only prompt, so the developer prefix diverged.
2. preamble (additional_tools / mcp_list_tools) — round-1 kept them at their layout positions via patchResponsesInput; round-2 omitted them entirely.

Result: the round-1 -> round-2 input prefix diverged from input[0], so the upstream prompt cache took a full miss on every compress re-request, and round-2+ silently lost instructions (system) and the Codex local tool declarations.

Fix: thread the ResponsesProjection (computed once in prepareResponses) through pickAdapter into the responses adapter. buildRequest now calls patchResponsesInput(projection, coreMessages) — the same function round-1 uses — so preamble + patched original messages keep their exact prefix by construction, then injects the developer message as [...systemParts, prompt] to match round-1. Headers (prompt_cache_key) are already preserved by runCompressLoop; only the body was rebuilt.

OpenAI Chat and Anthropic are unaffected (OpenAI keeps system in msgs; Anthropic uses cache_control markers) — only the Responses path changes.

fix(anthropic): preserve client system + cache_control in V2 loop re-request

Same class of bug as the Responses (Codex) fix in this PR.

Round-2 buildRequest for the Anthropic protocol overwrote the top-level system field with systemPrompt (compress prompt only). But anthropicToCore does NOT put system into msgs (only user/assistant/tool/reasoning), so the client's original system is unrecoverable from coreMessages. Round-1 (prepareAnthropic) computed systemOut = injectSystem(parsed, opts) = [client system text] + [compress prompt] via buildSystem (which also preserves the cache_control marker). Round-2 sent only the compress prompt.

Result: round-2 lost the client system prompt (persona/instructions) AND the system block content diverged from round-1, breaking Anthropic's prefix cache (the system block is the cache anchor) on every compress re-request.

Fix: thread the original parsed.system from prepareAnthropic through pickAdapter into the anthropic adapter. buildRequest now reconstructs system = buildSystem(extractSystem(original) + '---' + systemPrompt, original) — the same merge injectSystem uses in round-1 — so both the client system text and the cache_control marker survive and the prefix matches byte-for-byte.

OpenAI Chat is unaffected: its system is a role:system message that rides inside coreMessages and is re-emitted + merged identically by injectOpenaiSystem in both rounds.

Round N+1 of the V2 compress loop reused round-1's coreMessages, where a

fix(loop): restore re-request after compress + one-compress guard

Fix A (no re-request after compress) hung the session: the model emits a
compress function_call, the proxy executes it, but without re-requesting
the model never receives the result and never generates its actual
response → client sees a tool-call-only completion and stalls.

The re-request is the standard function-calling continuation (proxy acts
as the client: execute tool, feed result back, model continues). Restore
it for ALL proxy tools including compress/decompress.

To prevent the 0-char spiral (model re-targeting a just-compressed range
on a stale view in round 2+), add a one-compress guard: after the first
compress/decompress in a request, subsequent mutating calls return a
no-op result instead of re-executing. The model sees 'already compressed,

code_mode. Direct comfly A/B testing disproved this: declaring function tools
(top-level or additional_tools) does NOT disable codex's exec/code_mode tools.

- compress stays a text marker (batch ranges + immediate STOP is a poor fit
  for a single function call, and the marker path already works well).
- decompress/search_context/acp_status are now injected as real function
  tools so the model can call them directly (it often skipped emitting the
  text markers for these read-only tools).

The compress loop already merges text triggers and function tool_calls
(core.ts allCalls = [...calls, ...extracted.calls]), so both paths coexist
in one turn with no loop change.

- ACP_READONLY_TOOLS_RESPONSES: the 3 read-only tools (no compress).

fix(loop): cap acp_status at one call per request (prevent read-only run-on)

When codex calls acp_status as a function tool, some models (e.g. gpt-5.6-sol)
re-invoke it every round after receiving the result instead of emitting a
final answer, burning upstream calls until MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS. Observed in tmux
end-to-end test: 7 repeated acp_status calls (rounds 3-9) before the cap.

Mirror the compress mutatedThisTurn guard with a readOnlyCalled set: a second
acp_status in the same request returns a no-op ("Already called acp_status
this turn; the context status has not changed since. Generate your final
response now.") instead of re-executing.

acp_status is idempotent (no args) so capping at one per request is safe.
search_context is intentionally NOT capped — it takes a query arg and may
legitimately be called several times with different queries.

End-to-end (codex exec via bili 8788): with the cap, codex called acp_status
once in round 1, then emitted a clean final answer in round 2 (was: 7 repeats
hitting MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS=10).

function_call_output. The Responses API expects function_call ->
function_call_output pairing; a bare system message is ignored by the
model, so it re-calls the same tool (#119 run-on loop, hit MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS).

fix(loop): remove one-compress/readOnly guards — failure is the tool output (v10.txt)

The mutatedThisTurn (compress/decompress) and readOnlyCalled (acp_status)
guards short-circuited a SECOND call in a turn to a no-op. This was wrong:
the model may legitimately compress multiple different ranges, and a no-op
'Already compressed' message after a FAILED first compress was inaccurate
and sent the model into a retry spiral (v10.txt).

The real fix is f898da9: the proxy-tool result (success OR failure) is fed
back as a normal function_call_output (Responses) / tool-result (other
protocols). The model sees why a compress failed and decides its next
action — retry a different range, or stop. MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS bounds runaway.

Guard tests #11/#12/V1 rewritten to assert the second call now EXECUTES.

fix(compress): remove 'Do not retry' directive from failure result

The proxy-tool result must report the failure FACT only, not instruct the
model. 'Do not retry the same range.' was a directive the model followed
poorly (retried slightly-different ranges, looping). Per the principle
that failure is the tool output and the model decides its own next action,
the result now states only what failed.

fix(compress): strip kernel's 'Combine more messages' suggestion from failure

acp-kernel's min-range error appends a directive ('Combine more messages
into your range(s) to meet the threshold.') telling the model what to do.
Per the principle that the failure result reports facts only (model decides),
strip that sentence so the result is purely factual, e.g.
'Total compressible content too small (3955 chars across 1 range(s), min 5000).'

revert: keep kernel's 'Combine more messages' guidance in failure result

The kernel's suggestion ('Combine more messages into your range(s) to meet
the threshold.') is correct and helpful — it tells the model how to make a
retry succeed. Only the proxy's own 'Do not retry the same range.' directive
(removed in 6bad08b) was wrong. Restore the kernel message verbatim.

fix(loop): keep failed compress/decompress records visible (model can count attempts)

hideConsumedCompressCalls hid ALL orphan compress records — including FAILED
ones (no block created → orphan → hidden). The model then saw neither its
previous attempt nor the failure, so it reset to 'attempt 1' every round
and looped (tmux experiment: 10 rounds all '第 1 次尝试').

Only hide when no compress/decompress failed this round. A failed attempt
must stay visible so the model can count it and decide to stop.

fix(responses): pass non-proxy function_call items through raw

The Responses adapter previously swallowed EVERY function_call item
(added/arguments.delta/arguments.done/output_item.done) into a pending
map and re-emitted it via buildFunctionCallEvents with a NEW item id
(fc-proxy-...) and the arguments collapsed into a single delta. This
reconstruction is fine for proxy tools the loop must intercept
(compress/decompress/search_context/acp_status), but it corrupts the
wire format for real client-side tools: the streamed events use a
synthetic id while response.completed.output still carries the upstream's
original id, and strict clients that dispatch on the streamed lifecycle
(e.g. Codex multi-agent agents.* namespaced tools) reject the call
('unsupported call: spawn_agent').

custom_tool_call items already passed through raw; function_call did not.
This made namespaced function tools (agents.*) fail while custom-tool
based tools worked.

Fix: only intercept function_call items whose name is in PROXY_TOOL_NAMES;
all other function_call items are forwarded as raw meta (unchanged SSE),
exactly like custom_tool_call. A passthrough flag on the tool_call event
lets the loop count the call (so it still suppresses the re-request when
a real call was made) without re-emitting it.

(original item id + namespaced name + call_id + args preserved, no

first user message to 200 chars before hashing it into the session id.

a long system/context prefix or boilerplate precedes the real request)
collided onto one session id, cross-contaminating their compression
state.

The first user message is stable across turns (clients resend the full
history), and hashId streams sha256, so hashing the full content adds no
meaningful cost and eliminates the collision. conversationSignalResponses
already hashed the full input; this aligns the other two.

fix(responses): emit full item lifecycle on stream-error path; drop dead rewriter (#62)

preceding response.output_item.added, NO item_id, and NO output_index.

lifecycle would see an orphan + malformed delta and crash exactly when
the compress loop already failed — the user got a crash instead of the
error text.

output_item.added → content_part.added → output_text.delta → output_text.done
→ content_part.done → output_item.done, then response.completed with the
message item populated in output.

The happy-path streaming adapter was already correct (emitText/emitMarker
both route through buildMessageItemSequence, which always pairs
added+delta). Verification (via oracle agent trace):
 - server.ts:1325 streaming branch → pickAdapter → createResponsesAdapter
   → runCompressLoop; emitText/emitMarker/emitToolCall all emit
   output_item.added before their delta.

   imported at server.ts:50, zero call sites. Its orphan-delta sites

fix: self-heal context window on upstream overflow + arm emergency shrink

When the configured context window is wrong — most commonly the 200k
fallback for an unknown model on a private relay (the MITM case) — the
nudge/truncate bands sit far above the real window and the upstream 400s on
every turn. The proxy previously passed that 400 through verbatim with no
recovery, so a non-compliant model left the session permanently stuck
400-ing (the context blows up and the session stalls).

forward()'s non-2xx path now buffers the (small) error body and inspects it
for a context-overflow (inspectContextOverflow in src/util.ts — a pure,
tested helper: only 400/413 with a recognized context-too-long marker counts,
and it deliberately does NOT match Bedrock's "too many tokens" throttle
phrase, a 429 the client should back off on). On detection it:
  - learns the real window from the error body (OpenAI "maximum context
    length is N", Anthropic "X tokens > Y maximum", ...) and persists it to
    session.metadata.learnedContextLimit (a STABLE field — effectiveContextLimit
    is re-resolved every turn and would be overwritten);
  - handle() then self-heals: if the learned window is smaller than what was
    resolved this turn, it re-centers reqConfig.modelContextLimit on it (spread
    into a new object — never mutates the shared global config), so the
    nudge/truncate bands drop below the real limit;
  - arms an emergency shrink by raising lastInputTokens to the window (a lower
    bound — it overflowed, so the context is at least that big), so the next
    turn's usage is >=100% and the kernel's emergency nudge + tool-result
    truncate fire;
  - still passes the error through verbatim (no client-visible change).

Tests: tests/context-overflow.test.ts (11 unit cases) +
tests/e2e-overflow-selfheal.test.ts (overflow -> learn+arm+passthrough ->
recover, real usage report overwrites the armed value).

fix: reserve per-request output headroom from the context window

The kernel's nudge/truncate bands are a fraction of modelContextLimit, but
none of the layers reserved room for the model's OUTPUT. On a small window
(e.g. 100k) with a large max_tokens, context + output can exceed the window
and overflow before the nudge fires — the most common 'context blew up'
cause on a 100k window.

Reserve the request's exact max_tokens (the output budget for THIS turn)
from the window when handing it to the kernel, so the bands sit below
(window - maxOutput). Pure reserveOutputHeadroom() + per-request wiring in
handle(); unit-tested (4 cases). Complements the self-heal (reactive recovery)
with a preventive reservation — together they prevent + recover from the
context+output overflow.

fix: scope learned overflow window per model + broaden detection + cap error-body read

- Per-model learnedContextLimits: the learned window is keyed by the
  model that overflowed. Previously a session-level scalar capped the
  WHOLE session — after /model-switching to a bigger model mid-

fix(overflow-selfheal): persist learned window on the error path + protocol-aware headroom

Review fixes for the overflow self-heal:

1. markDirty on the error path: forward()'s non-2xx branch learns the
   window (metadata.learnedContextLimits) and arms the emergency
   (stats.lastInputTokens) but returns before forward()'s trailing
   markDirty — both mutations lived only in memory and were lost on
   restart, so the next overflow had to be re-learned. Schedule the save
   in the branch that mutates. Pinned by a scheduleSave spy in the e2e
   (on-disk assertions can't prove it: the prepare phase's debounced
   save serializes the live session after the mutation anyway).

2. Strip upstream content-length/transfer-encoding unconditionally on
   the error path: when readStreamToBuffer breaks the body (errBody
   null) the response ends with no body, and a content-length claiming
   bytes that never arrive leaves the client on a broken response.

3. Protocol-aware output headroom: Anthropic's Messages API enforces
   the input limit independently of max_tokens (separate output budget),
   so reserving maxOutput from the window shifted every nudge/truncate
   band down by maxOutput on every Anthropic session with no safety
   gain. OpenAI-family APIs count output against the window — reserve
   there (and for unknown protocols, conservatively). New
   shouldReserveOutputHeadroom() + unit tests.

fix(compress): accept JSON-string content in parseCompressInput

Non-strict-tool providers (e.g. vLLM openai-completions,
supportsStrictTools:false) stringify nested array arguments, so the model
may send compress.content as a JSON string instead of an array. Previously
Array.isArray(obj.content) was false and toRange(obj) returned null, so the
call silently parsed 0 ranges and compression never ran.

parseCompressInput now JSON.parse's a string content before the array check
(invalid JSON -> warn + 0 ranges, no crash), mirroring the fix in
billion-context-pi PR #164 (normalizeRanges in src/compress-tool.ts).

Adds a regression test for the JSON-string form.

fix: VSCode Copilot BYOK — total_tokens in final chunk + cancel propagation (#177)

Two VSCode Copilot BYOK bugs (issue #177):

1. Every response ended with "Cannot read properties of undefined
   (reading 'headerRequestId')". The proxy's OpenAI streaming adapter
   rebuilt the final chunk's usage from the loop accumulator and dropped
   total_tokens. VSCode Copilot's isApiUsage() requires prompt_tokens,
   completion_tokens AND total_tokens to all be numbers; without it the
   usage chunk was misclassified as a completion, so
   solution.requestId.headerRequestId threw. emitCompletion now emits
   total_tokens = inputTokens + outputTokens.

2. Clicking cancel mid-response left the proxy blocked waiting for the
   upstream, and the per-session lock stayed held so the whole session
   got stuck. The abort controller was created after the upstream fetch
   and its signal only reached the compress loop, never the fetch. The
   client-abort controller is now created before the fetch and its
   signal is passed to fetchWithTimeout (externalSignal) and the
   compress loop, so a client disconnect aborts the upstream request.
   The write loop also short-circuits when the response is destroyed.

Adds tests/vscode-copilot.test.ts with regression tests for both fixes.

fix(plugin): make /acp work in omp (persist conversation map + record prompt_cache_key)

Two fixes for /acp in omp (worked in pi from the start):

1. Persist the plugin-conversation map across proxy restarts. The
   conversationId->sessionId map in src/plugin.ts was in-memory only, so a
   fresh/resumed proxy had an empty map and /acp said 'no ACP session yet'
   until a new model request arrived. Now it is persisted to
   <stateDir>/plugin-conversations.json (debounced write on record, flush on
   the 3 shutdown paths, load after initSessions at startup).

2. Record omp's session id from the request body. The map is populated by
   recordPluginSession, called only inside 'if (pluginAgent)' — and
   pluginAgent comes from the x-bili-plugin header, which the plugin stamps in
   the before_provider_headers event. omp has NO such event (its dist only
   emits before_provider_request, body-only), so the header was never stamped
   and pluginAgent stayed undefined for omp. omp sends its own session id in
   the body as prompt_cache_key (a Responses-API field), which the kernel's
   conversationIdentityResponses already extracts as the conversation identity.
   Now, for responses requests with a client-provided identity, we call
   recordPluginSession(responsesIdentity.value, session.id) unconditionally —
   a no-op duplicate for pi, the only path for omp.

Verified: typecheck PASS, 526 tests pass, build PASS; e2e 'bili omp -p
<unique>' -> conversations file gains the omp session id, and
GET /__bili/plugin/status?conversationId=<id> returns ok:true with the

conversationIdentityResponses (acp-kernel/wire) does NOT read prompt_cache_key —

fix(loop): auto-retry acp-loop replay on transient upstream rejections (#189)

After a compress, provider risk-control may briefly reject the replay
request (GLM Coding Plan: 400 {"code":3007,"msg":"captcha verify failed"}
~1s after the context rewrite), and the error was passed straight into
the agent session. The replay request now retries transient upstream
failures with exponential backoff (3 attempts total, 1500ms base,
BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_BASE_MS override) on both the streaming loop and the
Responses-API JSON loop. Transient = 429/5xx or 4xx bodies matching
risk-control markers; plain 4xx still fail fast. Each retry logs a clear
"likely provider risk-control — retrying" line; exhausted failures are
surfaced with an "after N attempt(s)" suffix.

fix(loop): auto-retry acp-loop replay on transient upstream rejections (#189)

fix: survive upstream rejection of replayed thinking blocks in compress loop

After a proxy-tool round (compress/decompress/acp_status/search_context),
the loop rebuilds the conversation and re-requests upstream. The rebuilt
assistant message replays thinking blocks collected from the intercepted
turn. Two failure modes halted the agent right after the ACP marker
(upstream issue #221, MiniMax M3 via Anthropic-protocol relay):

- signature-less thinking (relay never sends signature_delta) cannot be
  replayed on Anthropic-protocol endpoints that validate -> 400
- even signed thinking replay is rejected by some relays/converter
  backends

Both made the loop emit an error and end_turn, so the agent stopped
executing right after the ACP tool result.

Fixes:
- proactively drop signature-less thinking segments from the replay
  (they are already streamed to the client verbatim in round 1)
- if the re-request is rejected with a 4xx, retry once with all
  loop-injected thinking blocks stripped (degraded retry, at most one
  per turn) before surfacing the error

Fixes https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/221

merge master: reconcile thinking-strip degraded retry with fetchWithRetry

PR #190 added fetchWithRetry (transient 429/5xx/risk-control replay retries,
BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX opt-out) to the re-request path. Keep that machinery
and layer the #221 fix on top: a deterministic 4xx that survives transient
retries triggers one degraded retry with loop thinking blocks stripped
before the error is surfaced.

fix(loop): strip model-emitted render tags to break #206 echo feedback loop

Models sometimes imitate the render tags injected into compressed history
and emit them in visible output. The client stores the echoed tags, replays
them next turn, and the imitation amplifies into unbounded repetition (#206).

Strip render tags from outgoing text in all three wire adapters (streaming
and non-streaming) with a streaming-safe filter; underscore-namespaced
text-protocol triggers and ordinary prose pass through untouched.

fix: persistent overlay homes for pi/omp/hermes launchers (session history loss)

The pi/omp/hermes launchers built their /bili/-rewritten config inside a
mkdtemp temp home (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR / HERMES_HOME) and rm -rf'd it when
the client exited. Clients persist absolute session paths derived from that
temp home into shared state (e.g. omp ~/.omp/agent/terminal-sessions/pts-*
resume pointers), and any file the client created directly inside the temp
home (agent.db, models.db, ...) was destroyed on exit — making omp session
history invisible and leaking temp dirs when the process was killed.

Replace temp homes with stable persistent overlays next to the real home
(~/.omp/agent-bili, ~/.pi/agent-bili, ~/.hermes-bili): every launch
refreshes entry symlinks (dropping dead ones, merging overlay-created
entries that shadow real-home entries back into the real home) and rewrites
the generated config atomically. The overlay is never deleted, so paths
stayed resolvable across runs.

opencode/claude/codex launchers are unaffected (env/temp-file only).

data could be silently destroyed instead of merged back into the real home:

  merge silently while the caller still rm'd the shadow subtree

both sides (mtime-newer-wins for files, losers kept as

fix: surface truncated upstream streams instead of silent end_turn

Follow-up to #221 (PR #222): the reporter still sees the agent stop
while outputting a long conclusion. If the relay drops the SSE stream
mid-generation (before message_delta/message_stop), the loop received
no done event, finishReason stayed undefined, and emitCompletion
defaulted it to a clean end_turn — the client then ended the turn
mid-text with no indication anything went wrong, which reads as the
agent silently stopping.

Detect the abnormal termination (no done event in the round) and emit
an explicit [acp-proxy: upstream stream truncated (...)] error block
plus an error-level log, so truncation is visible and diagnosable
instead of masquerading as a normal turn end.

Refs https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/221

fix: recognize Codex context-overflow errors and learn conservative window when unparseable

closes #280

After a macOS sleep/wake (or any rebind), a restored session starts with
lastInputTokens=0, so the nudge is blind and only the preflight fit check
can catch an oversized replay. Two gaps left the Codex path stuck:

- Codex's overflow error (code context_window_exceeded / "ran out of room
  in the model's context window") matched none of CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS,
  so no self-heal ever armed and the same oversized payload was re-sent
  forever.
- Even when the error is recognized, Codex's body carries no window number,
  so parseOverflowWindow found nothing and the floor stayed 0.

Now: both Codex markers are recognized, and when no window is parseable the
proxy learns a conservative window from the rejected payload's own size
(only-shrink-never-grow). The next turn's self-heal re-centers the limit
and preflight compresses the history below it before forward.

Tests: 2 unit (Codex error recognition) + Codex e2e self-heal (400 without
window number -> learned window -> preflight fold on the retry) + new
Responses-protocol e2e for the issue's suggested restore scenario (fresh
session, lastInputTokens=0, raw history over the window -> preflight
compresses before forward). Full suite: 661/661 pass.

fix: detect chained bili instances via x-bili-hop marker (#300)

When two bili instances are chained (A forward -> B), both run the
compression pipeline on the same request, double-compressing and
corrupting session state (root cause of #292).

- Outbound: stamp x-bili-hop: <instance-uuid> on every request this
  instance actually processed (main forward + preflight summarization +
  compress-loop calls via shared headers). A passthrough forward does NOT
  claim processing, so a dumb-proxy bili in front of a processing one is
  unaffected; any inbound marker keeps propagating down the chain.
- Inbound: if a request already carries x-bili-hop, an upstream bili already
  processed it. Skip ALL processing (no tool/tag injection, no acp-loop, no
  session state) and pass it through verbatim, logging a prominent [warn]
  naming the upstream instance (self-loop vs foreign chain).
- e2e: two tests — B in isolation with a foreign marker (body reaches the
  LLM byte-identical, no tool/tag injection, marker propagated), and the full
  A->B chain (single-layer processing, B warns, one LLM request, marker is
  A's not B's).

Clients never send this header, so single-instance use is unaffected.

fix: honor anthropic-beta context-1m to size the context window

When an Anthropic-format request carries an anthropic-beta header with a
larger-context beta (e.g. context-1m-2025-08-07), the client has negotiated a
1M-token upstream window. The proxy now sizes its own context window to match
(1,000,000), overriding the model-table default (200K for claude).

The beta is the most direct per-request evidence of the window the upstream
will serve, so it is resolved at the top of the native-window cascade and
re-read on every request (the header may appear/disappear between requests of
the same session). This fixes EMERGENCY / nudge / usage bands firing against
the wrong denominator — e.g. 261K input was 131% of 200K (EMERGENCY) when it
was really 26% of the 1M window the client negotiated.

- anthropicBetaContextWindow(): parses context-Nm betas (N x 1,000,000),
  largest wins.
- e2e: EMERGENCY suppressed at 261K input under the 1M beta; fires at the same
  input without the beta (200K). Plugin effectiveContextLimit is 1M with the
  beta and drops to 200K when the header disappears (per-request).

feat: partition codex subagent threads by turn-metadata (PR-A of #316)

Codex (>=0.147) reuses the root session-id header on subagent threads, so
the legacy identity chain mapped every thread of one task onto a single
session — subagents inherited the root's compression state, breaking #150's
isolation (a guardian subagent must read the user's original authorization
verbatim, never a compressed summary).

Add codexTurnIdentity(): when x-codex-turn-metadata is present and
cross-checked (metadata.thread_id === thread-id header), partition by
thread_source — "user" keeps the session-id header (current root
semantics, stable across turns), "subagent" gets its own thread-id (fresh
independent state per thread). Untrusted metadata (absent / unparseable /
mismatched / unknown thread_source) falls through to the legacy chain
unchanged, so no-metadata clients (omp pck, etc.) see zero regression.

The trusted id enters the verbatim session chain directly (no hashing, no
new dimensions) and bypasses subagentNamespace, leaving the kernel's
empty-instructions non-anchoring path untouched for metadata-less clients.

feat: anonymous tail-window reattach + fork lineage for prefix affinity (#316 PR-B)

A client that drops its oldest messages (truncation) previously failed the
full-depth prefix match and was orphaned into a fresh pfa- session, stranding
the old session's compression blocks. resolve() now falls back to a
tail-window comparison: the incoming's leading items are matched against each
stored chain's trailing items (position-independent per-item hashes), so a
truncated replay reattaches its original session and the kernel reconciles by
message id (verified: blocks deactivate gracefully on truncation and revive on
full replay, no throw).

New pfa- sessions also record a best-effort lineage (discarded candidates +
reason truncated/forked) in session metadata for UI/debug only — never used
for matching. Live-edge overwrite semantics unchanged.

fix(#377): re-voice mid-stream acp_summary as user messages (user-carrier)

Replace hoistMidSystemMessages (hoisted mid-stream system messages to the head
as separate system messages) with systemToUser (converts them to role "user",
leaving them at their anchor position).

Why: strict OpenAI-compatible backends (SGLang) require exactly ONE system
message at index 0 and reject a mid-conversation or second system message with
400 "System message must be at the beginning" (#377). The kernel renders each
compressed block's summary as role "system" anchored mid-conversation; in proxy
mode (plain client) the compress tool call is ephemeral and preflight blocks
have none, so the acp_summary is the only carrier. Re-voicing it as a "user"
message satisfies SGLang's one-system rule AND keeps the head system message
(the prefix-cache anchor) byte-stable across compress turns — a new block no
longer invalidates the whole-conversation prefix.

In plugin/launcher mode the summary carrier is the compress tool call (in the
agent's own re-sent history), so the kernel's acp_summary is stripped by
stripKernelSummaries and systemToUser is a no-op there.

fix(#437): make upstream timeout idle-based so long healthy streams aren't truncated

that only cleared once the body was fully consumed. A healthy stream that
legitimately runs longer than 10 minutes (e.g. a DeepSeek generation via
bili dsh) was aborted at the 10-minute mark mid-stream: the for-await loop

conversation truncated.

the timeout is IDLE-based during streaming: healthy long streams survive,
while a genuinely stuck stream (no chunk for timeoutMs) still trips the abort.

are preserved and callers see an identical Response shape (status/headers/body).

feat: detect + retry fake completions (tool call written as text, #371)

A small model (e.g. MiniMax-M3 via a gateway) can write a tool call as plain
text - echoing the tool-call XML template from the context - instead of
emitting a real tool block. With no tool block the agent ends the turn early
and shows success, but the tool never ran (the "fake completion" from #371,
root-cause follow-up to #361).

Add a proxy-side detect + retry fallback:
- Detect: a response carrying a complete tool-call structure (an opening
  invoke-style tag, or 2+ distinct closing tags) AND no real tool block for
  the wire protocol (Anthropic tool_use / OpenAI tool_calls / Responses
  function_call). Reuses PR #365's containsToolCallXmlFragment detector; the
  structural guard avoids false-positives on legit prose that merely mentions
  a single closing tag.
- Retry: re-request upstream with a corrective hint appended as a trailing
  user message. Bounded per turn (max retries) and per session
  (session.metadata.fakeCompletionStreak, resets on a clean turn).

Opt-in (disabled by default): the fallback must buffer the whole response
before the client sees it (a fake completion is only knowable at end-of-stream),
which defeats incremental streaming. That cost is only worth paying for the
low-frequency case, so it is opt-in via BILI_FAKE_COMPLETION_RETRIES (default
0 = pre-#371 passthrough).

Codex's native remote-compact request ends with a compaction_trigger

compress nudge injection appended a user message after it, so any
nudge-armed session that hit a native compact got
400 "The 'compaction_trigger' item must be the final input item."
and the pre-sampling compact (and the turn) failed.

Skip the nudge when the final input item is a compaction_trigger —

closes #280

After a macOS sleep/wake (or any rebind), a restored session starts with
lastInputTokens=0, so the nudge is blind and only the preflight fit check
can catch an oversized replay. Two gaps left the Codex path stuck:

- Codex's overflow error (code context_window_exceeded / "ran out of room
  in the model's context window") matched none of CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS,
  so no self-heal ever armed and the same oversized payload was re-sent
  forever.
- Even when the error is recognized, Codex's body carries no window number,
  so parseOverflowWindow found nothing and the floor stayed 0.

Now: both Codex markers are recognized, and when no window is parseable the
proxy learns a conservative window from the rejected payload's own size
(only-shrink-never-grow). The next turn's self-heal re-centers the limit
and preflight compresses the history below it before forward.

compresses before forward). Full suite: 661/661 pass.

PR #190 added fetchWithRetry (transient 429/5xx/risk-control replay retries,

After a proxy-tool round (compress/decompress/acp_status/search_context),
the loop rebuilds the conversation and re-requests upstream. The rebuilt
assistant message replays thinking blocks collected from the intercepted
turn. Two failure modes halted the agent right after the ACP marker
(upstream issue #221, MiniMax M3 via Anthropic-protocol relay):

- signature-less thinking (relay never sends signature_delta) cannot be
  replayed on Anthropic-protocol endpoints that validate -> 400
- even signed thinking replay is rejected by some relays/converter
  backends

Both made the loop emit an error and end_turn, so the agent stopped
executing right after the ACP tool result.

Fixes:
- proactively drop signature-less thinking segments from the replay
  (they are already streamed to the client verbatim in round 1)
- if the re-request is rejected with a 4xx, retry once with all
  loop-injected thinking blocks stripped (degraded retry, at most one
  per turn) before surfacing the error

fix: archive blocks across omp native compaction instead of silently deactivating them (#395)

omp's in-session native compaction re-sends a shortened history (its summary +
retained tail) without rotating the session id, so bili's per-sid registry
reuses stale state and syncBlocks silently deactivates every block whose raw
ids left the history — making decompress permanently unreachable and decoupling
acp_status from the real visible context (the ledger break #19 shelved).

Wire the omp session_compact hook bili was ignoring:
- agent plugin (pi/omp) POSTs /__bili/plugin/compact on session_compact
- proxy marks a compaction boundary; the next processTurn degrades the
  active->inactive blocks into an auditable pre-compaction archive
- acp_status lists archived blocks with reason; decompress returns an explicit
  error instead of silent failure or wrong-block content
- prune byRaw/byRef to live raw ids at the boundary (stops the #390 additive
  leak); nextIndex is left alone so a freed ref slot is never re-allocated onto
  a retained tail's live tag

fix: bili pi launcher disables pi's native auto-compaction (#447)

The `bili pi` launcher never disabled pi's own context compaction, so pi's
native summarizer (shouldCompact, enabled by default) could fire ahead of /
alongside bili's ACP compression and lossily rewrite the context bili is
managing — losing the detailed history.

The pi overlay (<piHome>-bili) is now ALWAYS built when the real pi home
exists and always carries a settings.json with compaction.enabled=false
(merged over the user's real settings.json, which is never mutated). This
makes bili's ACP compression the sole compression path under `bili pi`,

had preflight as a backstop, but its trigger estimate (estimateCoreMessages)
ignores system+tools and can lag by a turn, so it missed the overflow.

  max_output_tokens) to window - estimated_input - margin so input+output can
  never exceed the window on request-rebuilding upstreams. Anthropic is exempt
  (its input limit is independent of max_tokens). estimateInputTokens takes the
  max of the real previous-turn input and a fresh count that includes system +
  tool definitions, closing the undershoot that let preflight skip.
- Escalate the nudge: force-inject every turn once usage >= EMERGENCY_NUDGE_
  ESCALATION_PCT (0.70) even when the kernel's cadence/growth gate stays silent.
  The kernel already auto-injects above nudge.maxContextLimitPct (default 0.75),
  so the line sits just under it to fill the pre-limit silent climb. diagNudge

fix: echo reasoning_content on acp-loop re-request for non-Anthropic upstreams

The acp-loop re-appends the current round's captured thinking to the
re-request after a proxy tool runs. Its guard skipped any segment lacking a
signature:

    if (seg.text.length === 0 || seg.signature.length === 0) continue;

Signatures are Anthropic-only. OpenAI/DeepSeek thinking mode emits no
signature and instead requires reasoning_content echoed back verbatim, so this
condition dropped every such round's reasoning from the re-request — leaving
the assistant message that called the proxy tool without reasoning_content.
DeepSeek rejects that with 400 invalid_request_error ("reasoning_content ...
must be passed back"). A compress re-request was unaffected because it goes
through refreshFolded (#422), which rebuilds from fresh sidecars.

Gate the requirement on protocol, relaxing ONLY for the known non-signature
protocols:

    const requiresThinkingSignature =
        ctx.protocol !== "openai" && ctx.protocol !== "responses";

Anthropic (and an unset protocol) keep the strict #221 posture — dropping
unsigned thinking never 400s, keeping it can. This matches the existing
core.ts usage convention where unset already defaults to Anthropic-like
accounting (ctx.protocol === "openai" || ctx.protocol === "responses").

fix: tool-carrying main requests with a client-starved output budget no longer demote to side requests (#546)

Clients that size the output budget from their raw (uncompressed)
history (dsh) drive max_tokens/max_completion_tokens/max_output_tokens
down to <=200 tokens on long sessions, which tripped the #388
side-request heuristic: the main turn was forwarded as a pure side
passthrough, skipping processTurn/preflight/compression entirely, and
the reply truncated to a handful of tokens — a feedback loop the
session can never escape (the model cannot even emit a compress tool
call).

tools array marks an agent main turn; title-gen side requests never
carry tools):

  starved main request always re-enters the pipeline.
- restoreOutputBudget (run before the side gate) remembers the
  session's healthy output budget (last non-starved value, persisted
  via session.metadata) and restores it in-place on the request body
  when a tool-carrying turn arrives with a starved budget, so the turn
  actually reaches the model with room to answer (and to call
  compress). Side requests (no tools) are never touched.

fix: break the small-model same-parameter compress failure loop early (#156)

Rebased onto current master (v0.1.84); core.ts had evolved (+168/-44 since
v0.1.65) but kept the same run-to-MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS behavior with no
repeat-detection, so the issue still reproduces on the live version.

A small model can get stuck re-submitting the EXACT same failing compress
call (identical args) every round. Compress validation is deterministic, so
an identical call fails identically — re-requesting only burns a real upstream
call for an identical result. Previously the loop ran to MAX_LOOP_ROUNDS (10
real upstream calls) before completing gracefully.

runCompressLoop (src/loop/core.ts) now tracks the canonical args of every
compress/decompress that fails this loop. If a round is ONLY failed
compress/decompress calls and one of them re-submits args that already failed,
the loop breaks early (graceful completion) instead of running to the limit.

- Match is on canonicalized args (parsed + keys sorted), so key-order/whitespace
  differences do not defeat it.
- Fires only when the model is doing nothing but repeating failures: a
  successful compress or any other proxy call in the round suppresses the break.
- The model still gets one full chance to see a failure and correct it (break
  fires on the SECOND identical submission, verified at round 2 in tests).

idle watchdog could fire, making that knob ineffective for exactly the
slow-prefill case it exists for.

undici's fetch layer ignores per-request bodyTimeout/headersTimeout, so the
effective lever is dispatcher-level:

fix: guard side requests against over-window payloads (#554)

Side requests (max_tokens<=200) bypass preflight by design (#388) and were forwarded verbatim regardless of payload size — a full-history side request over the upstream window is a guaranteed upstream 400 that the learned self-heal can never fix from that path (the gate fires before the self-heal read, the overflow marker was unrecognized, and the fallback estimate ran on an empty kernel view).

- sideRequestGuard: estimate the raw body (CJK-aware text + image tokens) against min(resolved, learned) window minus output headroom on non-Anthropic wires; block locally with 413 side_request_payload_too_large instead of forwarding

- overflow learning on side requests: recognize the llama.cpp-family exceed_context_size_error marker and parse its '(A / B > W)' window form; when the kernel view is empty (side path), fall back to the raw-body estimate so the real window is learned and the next identical request is blocked locally

fix: forward-proxy requests no longer misread as self, restoring per-upstream window config (#562)

resolveUpstream() decided "is this the proxy itself?" by comparing the
absolute-URL authority against the client-provided Host header. In a real
forward proxy the client sets Host to the UPSTREAM (== the URL authority), so
every legitimate forward-proxy request was misclassified as a self-request and
dropped to undefined — losing per-upstream context-window config
(route?.rewrittenUrl undefined) while the fallback forward still reached the
upstream (chat kept working, the window silently did not).

Every well-formed absolute-form request is now marked a tunnel and routed
through checkTunnelDestination, whose self-layer (destination port == our bound
port AND a local-machine IP) 403s a genuine self-forward before any forwarding —
no silent fall-through to the fallback path. Self-detection uses the actual
listening endpoint instead of the client-provided Host header.

Tests: forward-proxy (Host == upstream authority) routes as a tunnel; the
forward-proxy and /bili/ forms of the same upstream resolve the same model
window; a self-targeting absolute URL is denied with 403 instead of forwarded.

fix: keep Responses assistant history valid after compression (#564)

Folding removes the tool calls/results that separated two assistant turns, and stripKernelSummaries can then delete the acp_summary that was the last separator - merging two turns into one run that Responses rejects with invalid_assistant_history.

Add repairResponsesAssistantOrdering(), applied AFTER summary dedup at all three Responses wire-build sites (initial prepare, compact forge, compress re-request). It rebuilds turn boundaries from the ORIGINAL client history: drop a reasoning whose turn body was wholly folded away (keep originally-reasoning-only turns), otherwise separate merged runs with a neutral user marker. Signed reasoning items are preserved verbatim (encrypted_content untouched).

fix: bound close-side tag-echo tail so a malformed </acp can't eat following content (#644)

A model-echoed render tag whose close is malformed (the echoed </acp is
missing its closing >) used to make the close-side tail regexes swallow the
entire following real content: TRUNC_CLOSE and the PARTIAL_TAIL close branch
were unbounded ([^<>]*), so at flush() / in the streaming hold, </acp + all
following non-angle prose was held (up to TAG_OPEN_CAP) then dropped, leaving
only the bare ref. The client saw a marker-only turn and the agent stalled.

Bound the close-side tail to {0,32} (aligned with the existing LONE_CLOSE
bound): an over-long tail is released as content instead of held/dropped.
Genuine short truncated closes (</acp, </acp tokens at stream end) still
match and are dropped.

- TRUNC_CLOSE: /<\/acp(?:\s[^<>]*)?$/ -> /<\/acp(?:\s[^<>]{0,32})?$/
- PARTIAL_TAIL close branch: \x3c\/acp(?:\s[^<>]*)? -> \x3c\/acp(?:\s[^<>]{0,32})?
- tests: malformed close + content survives (non-streaming + every split
  position), short truncated close still dropped

test: cover the #644 incident shape (whitespace after the malformed close)

The original #644 tests use a malformed close with no whitespace after
the close tag; the unbounded close-side tails could only consume content
through the whitespace-anchored group, so that variant never triggered
the bug (verified: all three #644 tests pass on unmodified master). The
recovered Turn B stream had whitespace right after the close - add the
incident shape: stripAcpTags must keep the following content, and the
streaming filter must match stripAcpTags at every split position.

fix(mcp): recover tool calls when the shim's conversation id goes stale after host resume

Fixes #656.

Claude Code resumes fork a NEW session id after MCP children are spawned,
so the shim's env-captured CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID goes stale and every tool
call 404s with 'unknown plugin conversation' for the rest of the session
while the proxy keeps serving the conversation under the new id.

- mcp.ts: on that exact 404, adopt the proxy's most-recent active
  conversation (status?fallback=latest) and retry once. Identity-bound
  hosts only; BILI_MCP_NO_ORPHAN_ADOPT=1 opts out for multi-session setups.
- plugin.ts: status fallback now reports the RESOLVED conversation id
  (it used to echo the caller's stale id back, so adoption was impossible).
- plugin.ts: split the tool-endpoint 404 into its two real causes
  (never-registered id vs session-not-resident) and log the rejection -
  these 404s used to be invisible in bili.log.
- tests: fallback resolution + adopted-id tool call; never-registered
  wording assertion.

fix(#651): drop oversized reasoning from closed compress turns

Models that keep reasoning/thinking on the wire build a permanent
uncompressible floor: the fold anchor is a compress call, and any
reasoning sitting before that anchor survives every fold as protected
prefix. Storm sessions hit ~50% visible context lost this way.

Proxy-side twin of billion-context-pi #339 / opencode-acp #377:
- new src/reasoning-drop.ts: dropCompressReasoning() strips the
  contiguous reasoning run immediately preceding a CLOSED compress
  call (result present + genuine user message after) when the summed
  run exceeds a char threshold (default 2048). Active rounds, other
  tools' reasoning, and non-contiguous runs are never touched.
- resolveCompress() now merges a third nested-object field
  (reasoning) sub-field-wise like absorb/prompts.
- all three wire prepares (anthropic/openai/responses) apply the drop
  after stripKernelSummaries, before wire rebuild.
- new config: compress.reasoning = { drop = true, threshold = 2048 }.
- docs: CONFIGURATION.md + zh-CN; 17 new tests (1263 total green).

test(mcp): cover the identity-binding resume path for #656 stale-id recovery

The existing #656 test exercises the cooperative plugin protocol
(x-bili-plugin-conversation). Add a parallel test that drives the actual

identity register): a stale pre-resume id 404s, status?fallback=latest

docs: name the kill-switch use case — round-trip-requiring thinking models (#651)

fix(#651): close rounds on tool-result evidence, not user messages (#348 twin)

The 'genuine user message after the compress call' closure gate is
unreachable in long agentic sessions — no user messages exist after the
opening prompt, so every compress round stayed 'active' forever and its
thinking survived as a permanent uncompressible floor (observed on the
pi side: 0 drops, 20.6K/8.4K/10.6K chars retained).

A round now closes when the compress call's tool-result (contentType
'tool-result', matching toolCallId) exists at a later index AND at least
one message follows it. In-flight rounds (result missing, or result
still the last message) are never touched; the per-provider
compress.providers.<name>.reasoning.drop=false escape hatch is preserved
for reasoning-replay providers (GLM).

rewritten with round-evidence scenarios (no-user-message agentic chains,

special UA) fell through every #408 backfill exemption (pi/omp by
