fix: preflight learns to drop max_output_tokens when the upstream rejects it

Responses-API preflight summaries unconditionally sent
max_output_tokens: 8192. The Codex backend
(chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses) rejects that parameter with
400 {"detail":"Unsupported parameter: max_output_tokens"}, so every
over-window request died with a 502 that no client retry could recover.

Follows the existing #626 stream-required capability-learning pattern:
only an explicit HTTP 400 naming max_output_tokens causes Responses
summaries to omit it. Learning is scoped to session + upstream URL +
model, so standard Responses providers keep the 8192 output limit.
Both rejection orders (stream-first / param-first) are covered and
compatibility retries are bounded (each capability learned at most
once, <=3 attempts per range).

Adds tests/preflight-max-output-tokens.test.ts: both rejection orders
against a mock Codex-like backend (summary generation + recovery +
forwarding + second-request first-shot compatibility), a standard
provider that retains the cap, and model-scoped learning.

fix: drop the Codex Lite header from preflight summary calls

The independently built Responses summary body has no reasoning field, but

fix(launcher): cross-process startup-window race — starting marker prevents double-spawn (#707)

fix(launcher): make the O_EXCL claim the arbiter — close read→claim TOCTOU and deadline-boundary sliver (#707 review)

Two residual double-spawn windows in the starting-marker protocol, found in review:

1. The pre-spawn readStartingMarker() was treated as the coordination
   decision while the O_EXCL claim result was ignored: two processes that
   both read 'no marker' before either claimed would each spawn (the loser's
   EEXIST was dropped on the floor). The default port-0 path widens the
   window with await pickEphemeralPort() between read and claim. Now a
   claim loser re-reads the marker: active holder → wait for it (same probe
   as attach); stale/garbage file → remove and re-claim once; still losing →
   degrade to pre-#707 spawn. This also self-heals an unreadable marker file
   (crash mid-write), which previously blocked every future claim forever.
2. The wait loop's deadline coincides with the starter's own poll deadline:
   a starter succeeding in its last ~200ms could be missed by the waiter's
   final poll, which then fell through to spawning a duplicate. The success
   path clears the marker, so the miss is indistinguishable from a failure
   bail without one more look — waitForStarterInstance now ends with a final
   probe after the loop exits.

fix: repair strict-echo reasoning on the compress-loop re-request path (#762)

The #763 normalization ran only in prepareOpenai, but the compress-loop re-request is built by adapter.buildRequest from the kernel view and bypasses prepareOpenai entirely. Move the two helpers to src/strict-echo.ts (leaf module: loop/* must not import server.ts), add a body-level normalizeStrictEchoBody, and apply it in runCompressLoop after buildRequest, gated by the same learned-flag/static-origin predicate.

fix(responses): keep tool call/output pairs adjacent on the wire (#766)

Strict Responses backends (DeepSeek) reject a request whose function_call_output does not directly follow its call group: a message/reasoning item wedged between a call and its output yields 'No tool output found for tool call <id>' even though both items exist, permanently wedging the session until the client history is dropped.

Root cause: surfaceReadonlyJson appended the acp_status visibility marker as an assistant message AFTER a real function_call in the same response, so the client recorded [function_call, message, function_call_output].

- New src/tool-pair-order.ts: hoistTrappedToolItems() hoists any non-tool item trapped between a call and its matching output to just before the earliest trapping call. No-op (same array ref) on healthy input, so well-formed sessions stay byte-stable for the prefix cache.
- Enforce at every Responses input-build site: unified streaming buildRequest (adapter-responses.ts), non-streaming prepareResponses (server.ts), and the legacy JSON replay (compress-loop-responses.ts). This also heals already-poisoned sessions without dropping the jsonl.
- Fix the root cause in surfaceReadonlyJson: insert the marker before the first tool call instead of appending after.

fix: auto-retry invisible degenerate terminal turns (#732)

A reasoning model can end a turn with ONLY a thinking block — zero visible
text, zero tool calls, status completed — most often right after a
post-compress re-request, where it sees the freshly-shrunk context and
"wraps up" into a silent thought. The client then receives an empty completed
turn and stalls until manually nudged (#732).

#673/#674 shipped the [degenerate-turn] detector as "the groundwork for
auto-retry" but never implemented the retry. This adds it: when nothing has
reached the client yet (forwardedAny=false — true for these rounds on wires
whose round>1 framing is suppressed, e.g. Responses) and the turn is a genuine
silent thought (sawThinking, not a legitimately empty/no-reasoning terminal),
re-fetch once with an ephemeral continuation nudge. One-shot per request; the
nudge is never committed to session state.

fix: request-scoped idle watchdog, malformed-body 400 guard, stale-install reminder dedupe (#806)

Three fixes for the incident reported in #806:

1. Request-scoped IDLE watchdog (main bug): an accepted request that
produces no output for the budget now ends in a 504 gateway_timeout
instead of hanging the client forever. Armed at accept time (before
prepare), re-armed on every response write, cleared on close. Default
budget is 2x the upstream idle timeout (24 min); override or disable
with BILI_REQUEST_WATCHDOG_MS. Firing also aborts the request's
upstream fetch (registered via WeakMap at both clientAbort sites) so
the per-session lock releases promptly instead of being held until the
upstream timeout fires. Covers /bili/ and MITM paths alike, since both
enter through the same createServer handler.

2. Malformed-body guard (secondary bug): a parseable body missing the
required "messages" array used to crash inside the acp-kernel
conversation-signal fingerprint (unguarded body.messages.find in
conversationSignalAnthropic/conversationSignalOpenai) and surface as a
502 "acp-proxy failure". Such bodies now get a 400 invalid_request_error
in the wire-native shape before reaching the kernel. Unparseable bodies
keep their raw-forward behavior. Hard-failure logs now include a capped
stack trace for faster triage.

3. Stale-install reminder dedupe (tertiary bug): the "restart bili to
activate" warning repeated identically every check cycle; it now logs
once per version pair. The decision was extracted to reportNotNewer()
because checkForUpdate's source-checkout guard blocks in-repo e2e
testing of that path.

Tests: new tests/fix-806-request-watchdog.test.ts (env parsing,
silent-upstream 504, streaming re-arm proving idle-not-total semantics,
fast-response no-op), new tests/fix-806-malformed-body.test.ts (400
shapes for both protocols, top-level array body, valid passthrough,
raw forward preserved), extended tests/update-restart-reminder.test.ts
(+4 cases). Pre-flight: typecheck clean, build ok, full suite green
(1526 tests, 0 fail, 2 skipped = gated e2e).

fix: stop image estimates poisoning the usage baseline (#857)

On non-pixel-billing upstreams (DeepSeek et al.) the conservative bytes-mode
image estimate (base64/4) overestimates real image billing by ~100x. That
estimate leaked into session.stats.lastInputTokens via the preflight fold
write-back (and the same-class #604 failure arming / weak-overflow arming),
then masqueraded as upstream-accepted evidence:

- the upward window self-heal CONFIRMED the inflated baseline as the model's
  real window (1,000,000 -> 1,072,519 in the issue's logs), and
- the #496 escape hatch stayed permanently closed because "baseline >= window
  + a learned limit" read as overflow evidence.

A DeepSeek session with screenshots then 502-loops forever despite ~50K real
input.

Fix:
- C1: the preflight write-back persists text+overhead only; the image floor
  is excluded (every fit/clamp gate adds its estimate separately).
- C2: new optional stats.lastInputTokensSource ("usage" | "estimate") tags
  every baseline raise — usage reports stamp "usage", local estimates stamp
  "estimate", derivative adjustments preserve the flag. Persisted through
  SessionStore; absent on legacy files = untrusted.
- C3: the upward window self-heal and stale-limit retraction trust
  "usage"-grounded baselines only.
- C4: the #496 hatch no longer treats an estimate-derived or legacy-unmarked
  baseline as overflow evidence, and a learned limit ABOVE the configured
  window (upward-self-heal residue that never applied) no longer counts.
  Genuine overflow still hard-fails (byte-relay protection intact; #767
  regression covered).

Legacy sessions already poisoned by the old code recover automatically: their
unmarked baseline reopens the hatch, one forwarded turn is accepted by the
pixel-billing upstream, and the next usage report snaps the baseline back to
reality (manual cleanup: delete the session file or its
metadata.confirmedContextLimits entry).

fix(config): generic family guesses default to 200k window instead of 128k (#852)

Owner directive in #852: unidentifiable models should fall back to 200k,
not 128k. The generic family-guess table entries (glm- catch-all, qwen,
kimi, llama-) are revalued 128k -> 200k. Entries documenting a specific
known window keep their real value (gpt-4o / gpt-4-turbo / glm-4.6 /
deepseek legacy r1-v3-ocr at ~128k).

The ultimate fallback for a model found nowhere was already 200k
(config.ts modelContextLimit default), so this aligns the weak guesses
with it. Rationale is the existing asymmetric-risk argument: a too-small
guess strands the session in the preflight fail-fast loop, a too-large
one self-heals on the first upstream overflow. Registry/snapshot lookups
still outrank the table, so listed models resolve to their real windows
online; the table is the offline floor only.

fix(preflight): fold deep enough for a payload far over the window

A preflight folds one range per round and can spend a bounded number of
summarization calls, so a payload that is well over the window and split into
many ranges needs several rounds. Eight of each was not enough for the cases
that matter: a live Gemini session of 1.39M tokens against a 1.05M window had
every fold it attempted succeed and still came out ~8k short, then dropped the
turn with "the compress budget was exhausted after 8 rounds" — the session was
recoverable and the budget refused to recover it.

Both budgets move to 16, which the new test pins: a fixture whose fold needs
more rounds than the old budget allows is refused at 8 and forwarded at 16
(needs a fold deeper than one round, and stays bounded). The preflight is the
last resort before an outright failure, so a bounded doubling of its work is
cheaper than the failure it prevents.

fix(loop): swallow a render tag wrapped around the model's turn

A model imitating the render tag can write its whole turn — tool call
included — where the opening's attributes are still open, so the attribute
list never terminates and no close tag is ever written (recorded shape:
`<acp tokens="1" text="text` immediately followed by the turn's own
markup, architect session 01a0a0cb, 2026-09-16T17:29:09). Every tag pattern
misses the span at once: attribute classes stop at `<`, and the value opened
with a quote is never closed. The filter dropped the opening and released the
payload, and the agent received a completed turn of orphan
parameter/invoke/calls closers with no tool call in it, stalling until nudged.

The stripper now recognises the wrapped shape by form — the attribute list
runs into a `<` (BROKEN_ATTRS), or carries an odd number of quotes — and
swallows the span whole to a loose close tag or to the end of the turn, in
stripAcpTags and in the streaming filter alike, with a budget of its own so
the #644 rule for a plain opening's over-long tail stays intact. The turn
reaches the client empty, which the degenerate-turn retry (#870/#871) re-asks
for.

fix(preflight): report the post-fold size and remaining ranges in the fail-fast 502

The exhaustion path quoted the original tokenCount captured before folding,
so a 502 after 16 successful folds read as if nothing happened (the #868
incident: 1.39M -> 1.06M, still over the 1M window). The fail-fast now
reports the post-fold size ("~N tokens (down from ~M before preflight)") and
the compressible ranges still visible, via PreflightResult.rangesRemaining
tracked per round from the kernel's viable ranges; original phrasing is kept
verbatim when no fold ran. MAX_PREFLIGHT_ROUNDS is exported next to
MAX_SUMMARY_CALLS_PER_PREFLIGHT so tests derive budgets from constants.
New e2e case scales the round-budget fixture past the bound and pins the
honest 502 (round-budget wording, post-fold size, remaining-range count,
exactly one summary call per round, nothing forwarded).

docs(preflight): state the fold-depth coverage bound beside the budgets

Document next to MAX_PREFLIGHT_ROUNDS / MAX_SUMMARY_CALLS_PER_PREFLIGHT how
far over the window 16 folds can reach (one range per round x at most
CHUNK_FRACTION of the window per fold ~= 9.6x-window overshoot, i.e. a payload
up to ~10.6x the window, best case; lower in practice) and that beyond the
bound the loop still exits cleanly with the post-fold size and remaining
compressible-range count reported. Note that 16 is tuned to the #868 incident
class — an overshoot-scaled budget is deliberately left as a separate design

fix(plugin): retry a turn whose only visible output was a stripped tag echo

Plugin-mode turns that end with no visible text and no tool call reach the host
as an empty completed turn, which it then aborts (#673 logs them as degenerate).
The trigger is the render-tag echo: the model imitates the annotation line it saw
in its prompt, the tag filter strips it, and where the echo was the whole turn
nothing is left to send. The filter's own rules are not negotiable — #463 pins
that an all-echo turn is dropped, #673 pins that a typo'd tag never leaks and
that the emptiness is reported — so the turn is recovered rather than redefined.

The pipe re-issues the agent's own request once, with the continuation nudge
#732/#821 already uses for the compress loop, when a turn reaches its terminal
(openai finish_reason chunk, anthropic message_delta) with zero visible text, no
tool call and a clean completion reason. The retry's content is spliced into the
same client turn: the first attempt's terminal event is dropped, its message is
never re-opened, and the retry's anthropic content blocks are offset past the
ones the client already saw. A retry that also comes back empty, or cannot be
issued at all, leaves today's behaviour exactly as it was: the empty turn passes
through and [degenerate-turn] warns.

injectFakeCompletionHint's per-wire body mutation moves to wire-body.ts so both
post-hoc mutations share one implementation, and the retry nudge text moves to
degenerate-retry.ts so the loop and the pipe quote one string.

Harden the Responses plugin pipe with the degenerate-turn retry (#870, #732/#821)

The chat pipes re-issue the agent's own body once when a turn reaches its
terminal with nothing visible — the render-tag echo case the filter empties.
The Responses pipe had no such gate, so an echo-only codex subagent turn still
reached the host empty: 8 of one day's degenerate turns in a single session and
56 across all sessions.

Its terminal is a family rather than one event, so the retry HOLDS
response.output_text.done / response.content_part.done /
response.output_item.done until response.completed decides the turn. On a
degenerate completion the held events and that completion are dropped, the body
is re-issued with the same continuation nudge, and the retry is reframed onto
the ids the client already holds: its response.created and added events are
dropped, and item_id, output_index and the completed output ids are rewritten
to the first attempt's. A healthy turn releases the held events in place, so
holding never reorders a turn.

Wired at all three Responses passthrough sites (plugin mode, the native-compact
tee, and proxy mode without injection); the plugin chat pipes' refetch already
carries the URL and headers this needs.

fix(plugin): close the retry's abandoned reader, cover two tracing paths

Review follow-ups on #871.

The retry swaps in a new reader while the first attempt's stream is already
terminal and drained; the old one is now closed explicitly in both pipes
instead of being left for the garbage collector to release.

Two tests the reviewer asked for: a chunk that coalesces content with the
finish reason counts its own text (and, when that coalesced content is an echo,
still retries exactly once — the ordering the gate depends on), and a retry
stream that is cut still raises the #721 truncation signal, because takeover
resets the terminal flag.

fix(plugin): rewrite the Responses item id the client already holds

The retry reframed the response id, the completed output ids and the `item_id`
on deltas, but `response.output_item.*` carries the item's identity nested as
`item.id`. That frame is released to the client, so without this the client
watched the item it held be replaced by the retry's mid-turn.

Found by proving the pipe against the installed bundle rather than the build: a
Responses turn whose only output is an echoed render tag, driven through the real
CLI, reached the client with `item.id = msg_second` while every other id carried
the first attempt's. The regression pin now emits that frame from the retry.

fix(plugin): count a dropped tag's interior as degenerate output (#870, PR #871)

A render tag whose close never arrives is dropped by the filter while its
interior survives as the turn's only visible text: the host receives orphan
markup, finds no tool call in it, and stalls. The gate measured that interior
as visible output, so the degenerate-turn retry never fired.

Count the text a dropped tag leaves behind as markup instead, at both the chat
wire's rewrite sites, and re-issue the turn. The recorded architect-session
turn is the fixture, reconstructed from the client-visible residue because the
wire bytes are not kept anywhere.

fix(plugin): emit an in-band error when the retry degenerates too (#870, PR #871)

A turn the host never sees any content from is indistinguishable from a model
that produced nothing, and the client reports neither, so a dead session reads
as an idle one. The degenerate-turn gate already retried once; when that retry
degenerates as well, the client now gets the in-band stream error the host would
never surface, and the retry's own terminal is dropped so the error closes the
turn.

Observed on 2026-09-16 by the session that hit the corruption five times: no
parse error, no warning, the residue as ordinary assistant text.

fix(plugin): never retry a bare or trigger-final empty turn (#870, PR #871)

Two CI regressions found while reviewing #871's red test jobs:

1. The degenerate-turn re-issue fired on the native-compaction trigger
   request (the resetAfterSuccess passthrough), appending the continuation
   nudge AFTER compaction_trigger and breaking the wire shape (#283: the
   trigger must stay the last input item). makeContinuationRefetch now
   refuses to re-issue a body whose final input item is a trigger.

2. The new gates retried turns the model left genuinely bare — zero output
   of any kind — double-billing an upstream empty completion. Both plugin
   pipes now require proof of invisible-but-real output (a stripped
   render-tag/marker echo, released markup, or thought/reasoning), matching
   the boundary the compress loop has kept since #732/#821.

fix(launcher): strip inherited proxy vars from opencode launch env (#890)

The opencode branch spread the full process.env, so lowercase http_proxy/https_proxy/all_proxy inherited from the user's shell survived alongside the uppercase HTTPS_PROXY bili injects. undici (and Bun) resolve the lowercase form first when both are present, so model traffic was silently routed to the user's own proxy instead of bili — no processTurn/forward traces in the bili log while the session kept growing until the upstream rejected it on context overflow.

feat: search_context targets historical sessions read-only via conversation_id

Closes #841

fix: weak-overflow counts against demonstrated capability, not trusted-window usage (#901)

When the trusted window overstated reality, every overflow failure landed below the old >=90%-of-trusted gate and the conservative-window learner starved exactly where the deployment was broken (real sample: trusted 1M, true ~370k, all cuts at 60-96k never counted). Counting now keys off the largest input recent successful turns got through (recordProvenInput on genuine completions only); failures at or below it are instability noise and are dropped without consuming the event budget. With no success sample yet, capability is unknown and failures count, so an oversized first request under an inflated window stays learnable. The trusted-vs-demonstrated gap is exposed on /__bili/stats (contextWindow/provenMaxInput) and the web sessions page.

feat: add outbound size to request cost line; cover side-request guard block

- Log outbound= (wire bytes handed to forward()) so the inbound->outbound
  compression ratio is readable straight from the log; omitted on

- Cover the side-request guard-block exit (413), which the original five
  exit points missed.
- Count outbound via Buffer.byteLength: Prepared.body is string|Buffer and

fix(launcher,plugin-install): async spawn error + non-object mcp guards (#809 D/N4)

fix: TTL-cache the opencode-native per-request health probe (#928)

createNativeRoute probed GET /__bili/health (1500ms timeout) before every model request with no caching, while respawn in the same module is already rate-limited by RESPAWN_COOLDOWN_MS=15s. Per-request probing contradicted that stability assumption: a healthy proxy paid a loopback RTT on every request; a freshly dead one added up to 1.5s before degrading.

Wrap the probe in a per-origin TTL cache (HEALTH_PROBE_TTL_MS=2s, injectable via deps.probeTtlMs). Both verdicts are cached: a healthy hit removes the steady-state RTT; a dead hit avoids re-paying the timeout across the death+cooldown window. Stale entries are evicted on insert so the map stays bounded. Detection latency is bounded by one TTL, consistent with (and far tighter than) the 15s cooldown horizon.

Adds 3 regression tests: single probe across N steady-state requests, re-probe after TTL expiry (not a permanent latch), and death detected within one TTL degrading to direct.

fix: attach mode rewrites model URLs like spawn mode (#941 review)

The #941 stamp-only attach branch silently dropped compression for
OpenCode 1.x under `bili plugin install opencode` with a preset
BILLION_CONTEXT_PROXY/BILLION_CONTEXT_ATTACH and a provider without an
explicit baseURL: the V1 `server()` surface shares the module-level
intercept state (attach=true), and the V1 fetch patch is exactly what
used to route those SDK-default-baseURL requests into the proxy.

Attach now rewrites to `${origin}/bili/${url}` exactly like spawn
(#809 probe+rewrite semantics restored). For dsh under the `bili dsh`
launcher this is doubly safe: settings-overlay URLs are already
`/bili/`-shaped and take the routed branch (headers only), and rewriting
a raw upstream URL to the loopback proxy is never proxied by the MITM
envs (an http loopback target bypasses HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY forwarding
in every case that matters — worst case an absolute-form self-hop, which
the proxy unwraps normally).

  interface docs updated

  unchanged

fix: split Claude Code subagent sessions so they stop queueing on the main session lock (#970)

Claude Code stamps the same x-claude-code-session-id on every model request
of a session — Task-tool subagents included — so main turn and all subagents
land on ONE session and serialize on withSessionLock (which spans prepare +
forward + the whole streamed response). A slow subagent first token
head-of-line-blocks the main turn for the full upstream latency; observed
live as 116-142s first-byte stalls with two concurrent subagents.

Discrimination is two-signal, verified against live Claude Code 2.1.274
traffic (-p mode AND custom agent types like Explore): the request carries
the agent headers, AND the main agent's system-prefix block ("You are
Claude Code…" / "You are an interactive agent…") is absent — subagent
systems are their own agent definitions with no stable positive marker.
Both signals must agree; failure degrades to no-split (today's serial
behavior), never mis-splits the main session.

- src/session-id.ts: claudeSubagentAgentId / claudeSubagentSplit
- src/server.ts: anthropic conversation branch derives <id>|sub:<agent-id>;
  anthropicIdentity itself untouched (affinity/clientLabel stay continuous);
  split sessions can't claim the root's pending register (#317 mirror);
  recordPluginSession keys subagent sessions under the split id so the
  conversations map never flips between main and subagent sessions
- src/config.ts: BILI_SUBAGENT_SPLIT env gate (default on)
- tests: discrimination cases across captured system shapes, session
  isolation, deterministic no-stall (gated upstream), off-switch
- docs: CHANGELOG + CONFIGURATION (en/zh)

End-to-end verified: two concurrent Task subagents through the proxy land
on |sub: sessions and complete in parallel (20.6s vs 129-188s pre-fix).

fix: only an upstream-stated window is ever learned (#969)

A window number the upstream itself states in an overflow rejection
(confirmedContextLimits) is ground truth and stays learnable. Every
guessed size stops learning, because a persisted guess is how #969's
session shrank 18320 -> 16161 forever:

- 400 overflow WITHOUT a parseable window number learns nothing (was:
  the rejected payload's estimated size); the emergency shrink alone
  unblocks the next turn.
- noteWeakOverflow (3 mid-stream cuts / 15min) arms the emergency
  shrink but writes no learned* field, and never clobbers a confirmed
  window (already #570) nor refines its own old guesses.
- resolveLearnedLimit resolves confirmed evidence only; legacy
  speculative values in old session files stay inert (retraction
  still drains them).
- An operator-declared window (models.<id>.context /
  compress.modelContextLimit) is never overridden by a learned one.

  BILLION_CONTEXT_PROXY / BILI_PROVIDER_REWRITES set (bili claude launcher
  owns routing) → exit 0 immediately.

feat(proxy): serve the Google/Gemini wire

A Gemini request already reached the proxy (the MITM domain is configured) but
was forwarded verbatim: /v1beta/models/<model>:streamGenerateContent matched no
protocol, so the turn never entered a session and had no identity, folding,
compression or usage accounting.

- detection: googlePathKind()/googleModelFromPath() take the model from the URL
  PATH (Gemini carries it there, not in the body), protocol "google" is in
  KNOWN_PROTOCOLS with /bili/google/... as an explicit upstream prefix, and
  :countTokens is routed to a prune-only path.
- identity: conversationSignalGoogle, plus prefix affinity over `contents` for
  the anonymous case — omp stamps no session header for its google provider.
- prepare: prepareGoogle writes the system into body.systemInstruction (a Gemini
  request carries no system message in contents), injects the Gemini-shaped ACP
  tool declarations from the kernel, and merges a nudge into a trailing user
  content because the wire rejects non-alternating roles and a request must not
  end on the model side. Replayed reasoning keeps its thoughtSignature: unlike
  the other wires, a reasoning part is never dropped here, because Gemini 3
  validates the signature on every replayed part.
- loop: createGoogleAdapter + rewriteGoogleJsonResponse carry the compress loop
  on the streaming and non-streaming paths, including the tool-call signature
  and the googleThoughtSignature sidecar on replayed reasoning.
- aux pipes: preflight summary requests, in-band error frames, fake-completion
  detection, image-token counting, historical-image stripping and the plugin
  passthrough (usage sniffed from usageMetadata, finishReason-aware terminal
  handling, per-part tag-echo stripping with the same drop-and-warn behaviour
  the other two wires have).
- usage: promptTokenCount/cachedContentTokenCount in, candidatesTokenCount +
  thoughtsTokenCount out; gemini-3 added to the context-limit table.

Covered by tests/e2e-google-compress.test.ts (session-identified growth that

fix(preflight): read the summary reply a Gemini upstream streams regardless

A preflight on the google wire could never compress. summarizeRange opens the
summary call with stream=false (the #626 default for upstreams that answer a
stream call with JSON), but a Gemini summary goes to the client's own URL —
`…:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` — which answers SSE whatever the request
asks for: the Gemini payload has no `stream` field to turn it off. requestSummary
parsed SSE only when that flag was set, so the text of every summary reply was
discarded, the reply read as empty, and the whole per-request call budget (8)
was spent before the turn fail-fasted with "context ~N tokens exceeds the model
window … preflight compression could not bring it under: the preflight
summarization budget (8 calls per protection regime) was exhausted … the upstream
stream carried 41 SSE event(s) but no summary text" (#829).

The body's shape now decides how a summary reply is read, covering both
directions of the mismatch: a stream:true call answered with plain JSON (the
#626 case, unchanged) and a non-stream call answered with SSE (this one).

The Gemini extraction contract had no test coverage at all, which is what let
this reach a live session: tests/preflight-sse-extraction.test.ts gains the four
google cases (thinking parts skipped, lenient framing, mid-frame truncation,
in-stream error), and tests/preflight-google-summary.test.ts drives a real
over-window Gemini turn through the proxy against a mock upstream that answers
the way Google does — SSE for a streaming client, JSON for a `:generateContent`
client — asserting the summary replaces a raw range in the forwarded payload.

fix(loop): name the proxy tool result so the Gemini wire can answer the call

A proxy-owned tool call (compress, decompress, search_context, acp_status, absorb)
is answered by the proxy itself: it synthesizes the tool-call core AND the
tool-result core, then re-requests so the model sees the outcome. The call core
carried `toolName`, the result core only `toolCallId` — harmless on OpenAI and
Anthropic, which pair a result by id, but Gemini answers a call by NAME:
the wire emitted `functionResponse{name:"unknown"}` for a `functionCall` named
`compress`, and the API rejects the whole request with a generic
`400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("Request contains an invalid argument."), so an
anonymous Gemini session died on the first proxy tool call it made (#829).

The mock upstream in tests/e2e-google-compress.test.ts is now the strict one the
real API is: it validates every rebuilt request against Gemini's contract
(alternating roles, non-empty parts, exactly one payload per part, signatures
only on model parts, functionCall named, functionResponse named AND answering a
call seen earlier, response an object) and fails the test on any violation.
Reverting this one line reproduces nine `functionResponse name=unknown answers
no call (calls seen: compress)` violations; with it the suite is clean.

fix(loop/google): never forward a split text+functionCall chunk twice

A chunk carrying a text part AND a functionCall part is replayed whole at
settle, so its text must not also go out immediately. The guard counted only the
calls seen before the text part in iteration order, so `[text, functionCall]` —
the shape the reviewer named — forwarded the chunk as the text frame and the
settle replay forwarded it again, handing the client the text and the call
twice. The reasoning branch had no guard at all and had the same problem.

The edited copy the tag filter leaves behind had a second hole: it kept every
sibling part, so a PROXY call (which settle drops, because the proxy executes it
itself) rode out to the client inside the filtered text frame. The copy now
drops sibling call parts; settle replays them when they are real.

Covered by two tests: a split chunk delivering its text and its call once each,
and an edited frame carrying no proxy call. Reported by the maintainer's review
agent on PR #867 (finding 1); the cosmetic role on finish-only clones is fixed
in the same pass.

fix(loop): tolerate a null part when dropping sibling call parts

The guard that keeps a proxy call out of a tag-edited frame dereferenced every
sibling part, while the rest of the loop treats non-object parts defensively. A
malformed upstream chunk carrying a null part alongside tag-edited text therefore
threw mid-stream and took the turn with it.

Found in review of #867; the pin fails without this change.

fix(server): resolve backpressure wait on client disconnect so streams can't hang the session lock

Every stream-write backpressure wait used res.once('drain') only. When a
client stops reading mid-stream (dropped connection), 'drain' never fires:
the request hangs forever, the session lock chain never releases, and every
later request on that session queues behind it silently — the client sees a
stuck session that only a proxy restart recovers.

Replace all five waits with awaitDrain(), which also resolves on 'close' and
'error'. The stream loop then finishes (remaining chunks are dropped by the
closed socket), res.end() runs, and the lock is freed.

Verified: unit tests + a repro (client destroys the socket after 3 chunks;
before the fix the proxy never finishes, after it does).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: adopt parent compression blocks on anonymous fork detection (#629)

An anonymous (prefix-affinity) client that forks its history mid-conversation

compression state, losing every folded block that still lies fully inside the

fix: release held done-family events when the next item opens (#1061)

pipePluginResponsesWithStrip held response.output_text.done /
response.content_part.done / response.output_item.done until the
completion event decided retry, but forwarded
response.output_item.added immediately. With an upstream that emits
more than one reasoning item per turn (gpt-5.x interleaved thinking),
the client saw added(rs_2) before done(rs_1) — opencode v2 hard-errors
on that ordering (InvalidProviderOutput: started reasoning before the
previous item ended).

Fix: an opening output_item.added now flushes pending tag/arg tails
and all held done-family events first, restoring exact upstream
relative order for every item type. At the terminal event only the
last item's family can still be held, so the degenerate-turn retry
(#732/#821) keeps dropping exactly what it needs.

Secondary path in the same pipe: the retry stream's own
reasoning_summary_* frames were raw-forwarded with fresh ids whose
items were never announced (their added is dropped by retryFraming),
leaking ids the client cannot resolve. They are now suppressed with
the other retry framing events.

feat: bili→bili chain integrity — x-bili-sig digest + ACP-artifact fallback

A processing bili stamps x-bili-sig (sha256 of the exact emitted body bytes)
on every emission (initial forward, compat-role retry, fake-completion hint
retry); the receiving bili verifies it over the raw inbound buffer before any
processing. A mismatch means a middlebox rewrote the request — pass through
verbatim instead of processing content this instance did not produce. When a
relay strips bili's headers entirely, ACP artifacts in the body (render tags /
context-management tool names) trigger the same verbatim passthrough. Every
detection logs a [chain] line naming the signal that fired. Legacy chains that
carry only x-bili-hop (#300) behave exactly as before.

Related to #1078.

fix: side-request guard must not clamp on the host usage baseline (#1110)

The guard's effective window was fed session.stats.lastInputTokens whenever lastInputTokensSource was 'usage' — but that value is ALSO what a healthy compressed host turn writes as its nudge baseline. A low baseline (e.g. 3k after compression) permanently 413'd an unrelated in-process caller's fixed-size request (MemOS retrieval filter) even though it fit the model's real window, with no config/env escape hatch.

Decouple the two: add stats.overflowArmTokens, set ONLY by an upstream context-overflow 400 (the one-shot emergency arm per #554/#987) and cleared by the next real usage report and on compression reset. The guard reads overflowArmTokens, never the baseline. Existing overflow-arm e2e still pins the arm path; new e2e regression reproduces the 413 pre-fix and passes post-fix.

fix: make effectiveTokenCount's stale-high bound image-aware

The min-cap against the current request's inbound upper bound was
text-only (estimateCoreMessagesUpper sums m.text; wire codecs move
images out of CoreMessage.text into sidecars), so whenever the previous
turn's image contribution exceeded the current turn's text growth the
image term was capped away and the silent-backend nudge numerator went
blind to byte-billed multimodal sessions. Carry the current request's
image term (resolved billing) into the bound at all four call sites;
a client-side shrink shrinks the bound in both terms, preserving the
#728C stale-high invariant.

Fixes #1119

fix: resolve search_context conversation_id "current" to current session

The search_context conversation_id param description promises "Defaults to the
current conversation", but executeSearchContextTarget only special-cased an
empty id or one exactly equal to the session id — sending the literal "current"
fell through to the foreign lookup and failed as unknown session "current".
Resolve "current" (any case) to the current session so the documented default
actually works. Real session ids are generated (pfa-* / mNNNNN-style), so
shadowing a hypothetical session literally named "current" is negligible;
cross-session search for real ids is unchanged.

Fixes #1125

fix: conclusive compress failure receipt when conversation is below minCompressRange

When the WHOLE visible conversation holds fewer chars than compress.minCompressRange, no range combination can succeed (the kernel sums range chars against the single threshold), yet the standard failure receipt gave only generic 'combine more messages' advice — steering models straight back into compress retries and acp_status/search_context inspection loops (root-cause factor 3 of #1112).

Append one conclusive sentence to the applyRanges failure receipt when minCompressRange > 0 and total visible chars < minCompressRange: the floor is unreachable for any range, so do not retry compress or inspect ACP state about it. Kernel reason string and the #847 reversal note stay intact; when a viable larger range exists the generic advice is unchanged. No config schema change, no wire-shape change beyond failure-time tool-result text, plugin mode unaffected (receipt text only).

Piece 1 of the owner-approved split of PR #1121 (surface-gating half stays out of scope); re-applied standalone on current master per the split directive.

fix: runtime respawn for native attach mode when the shared proxy dies

A settings overlay bakes the launcher proxy origin into model request
URLs, so when the owning launcher of a SHARED proxy exits mid-session
every request from the attached client hits the dead port forever:
readyOrigin short-circuits on the frozen state.origin, and the death
branch required state.respawn which pure attach paths never armed.

- native-intercept: routed /bili/ requests now observe network failures;
  one recovery + one retry against the replacement origin, plus
  pre-emptive reroute of overlay-baked URLs for subsequent requests;
  when no replacement comes up, degrade to a direct send of the
  embedded upstream instead of failing forever. The rewrite branch
  shares the same recover() helper (stale origin cleared first).
- dsh-native: attach mode arms state.respawn = singleFlight(
  verifyAttachAndRecover(preset)) + onGiveUp, so runtime death
  re-probes the preset and falls back to spawn exactly like startup;
  the healthy path restores state.origin for the readyOrigin
  short-circuit.

fix: chain-detection content fallback exempts this instance's own sessions (#1086)

v0.1.133's content fallback judged bili's own injected ACP artifacts (render tags / acp_status+search_context tool surface) as bili->bili chain evidence and passed every turn through verbatim, so the compression kernel never ran again on single-instance setups (#1086). Re-introduces the fallback correctly after #1087's revert:

- structural detector: declarations alone are not artifacts; historical tool calls (both names, all four wire shapes) or wire-escaped render tags are; prose never counts
- self-state exemption: processed local state for the session (memory or persisted store) means the artifacts are self-produced, process normally
- foreign artifacts without local state: byte-identical passthrough, one warn per session, no session record created
- escape valve: chainContentDetection:false / BILI_CHAIN_CONTENT=0
docs: fix stray leading space breaking env-var table rows (#1086)

fix: skip ACP-artifact content fallback when persistence is disabled (#1100)

The chain-detection content fallback (#1086) decides "no local processed
state => foreign bili->bili chain => passthrough". That inference is only
sound when persistence can prove ownership across a restart: with
BILI_PERSIST=0 an instance cannot recover its session state after a
restart, so "no local state" is ambiguous with our OWN replayed session.
Treating it as decisive made a persistence-off instance permanently
pass-through every own session after a restart — compression silently off
and unbounded growth, i.e. the #1086 symptom again, scoped to
persistence-off + restart + replayed history.

Gate the fallback's byte pre-filter on getStore().enabled: when the store
is disabled the whole content fallback is skipped and the request is
processed normally. The x-bili-hop marker path is untouched and still
catches real chains. hasProcessedState already returned false in exactly
this case, but that boolean cannot express "decline to make a verdict", so
the decision belongs at the point where the fallback is gated.

Tests: T3 (foreign => passthrough) now runs an ENABLED store over an empty
temp dir so "no local state" is a sound foreignness signal; new T6 asserts
the BILI_PERSIST=0 + restart replay is processed, not passed through.

fix: drop mid-chain adoption from anonymous prefix affinity (#1115)

Tail-window reattach (#316) adopted a stored session when the incoming's
leading 8 per-item hashes hit ANY mid-chain offset of a tracked chain. A
mid-chain contiguous match is symmetric evidence, not an ownership proof: it
cannot distinguish 'same conversation, truncated replay' from 'a different
conversation quoting shared content' (templated tool outputs, standard files,
stock errors - parallel agents on one codebase produce these naturally), and
adoption was bidirectionally harmful (folded-summary leak to the adopter,
context pollution of the victim). The #1072 interim mitigation (full-8 window
instead of 3) closed sub-8 crafted windows but not the symmetry.

Three days of production logs (~11.5k anonymous resolutions) showed zero
tail-window reattaches and zero near-misses, so mid-chain adoption is removed
entirely (direction 3 of #1115): truncated replays now fork into a fresh
session. The truncated-run scan survives as lineage attribution only (never
matching): leading TRUNCATION_LINEAGE_WINDOW=8 run strictly inside a tracked
chain records lineage.reason='truncated' with all hit parents; a shared
leading prefix (LCP >= MIN_FORK_PREFIX=3) records 'forked' and takes
precedence. via narrows to 'prefix' | 'new'; the server tail-window log
branch is deleted.

Cost accepted: one raw resend + ladder restart per truncation (same cost class
as instruction-drift forks, #1106); opt-in block adoption (#629) still carries
fully-present blocks, kernel reconcile stays sound (deactivate/revive pinned).

Tests: tail-window-reconcile.test.ts renamed truncation-fork.test.ts and
rewritten (reattach assertions -> fork assertions; ambiguous multi-parent case
asserts attribution with both parents). New design record SESSION-IDENTITY.md
(+ .zh-CN): identity principles, threat model, measurement, rejected
alternatives, three-layer framework, future client-side identity signal.

feat: stable head-system anchor for prefix-cache preservation (#1085)

When a client's head system/instructions block changes mid-session (e.g. an embedded AGENTS.md is edited), the forwarded prefix diverges at byte zero and the provider's KV prefix cache misses in full. With stableSystemAnchor enabled (default off; env BILI_STABLE_SYSTEM_ANCHOR=1 or config file), bili freezes each session's first-seen head-system text as a sticky anchor and re-sends those bytes verbatim; detected changes are appended as trailing '[System context update]' user messages carrying the new full text, each superseding the previous ones. The anchor and append-only log live in session metadata (persisted, compaction-proof) and are re-injected every turn across all four wire surfaces (anthropic/openai/google/responses) including internal compress-loop rounds. Churn guard: more than 8 distinct changes replace the anchor outright (one deliberate cache miss). Excluded: title-gen micro-requests, Responses compaction-trigger requests, auto-mode classifier requests. Clients implementing their own variant of this mechanism need no extra injection — their in-history updates pass through as ordinary history (covered by test). On the responses wire, anchoring keys sessions on conversation identity alone so instruction drift no longer forks into orphaned |sub:<fp> sessions.

release v0.1.140

fix: watch the real claude host, not the transient sh hook wrapper

claude (2.x) runs SessionStart hooks as `/bin/sh -c <command>`: the hook's
direct parent is a transient sh that dies the moment the hook exits. The
spawned proxy's parent-pid watchdog was pointed at that sh, so it killed a
healthy proxy ~2s into EVERY session ("parent-gone (pid N)") while claude
itself kept running — every interactive claude session lost its bili proxy
and all subsequent model calls failed with Connection refused.

- resolveClaudeHostPid(): walk up from the hook through /proc (<pid>/cmdline
  for argv, <pid>/stat for ppid, zombie-safe), max 8 hops, and return the
  first ancestor whose argv is the claude session binary.
- isClaudeHostArgv() matches `claude`/`claude.exe` and node/bun/deno forms
  (`node .../@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js`, `node .../claude`); never the
  hook itself, `timeout 40 claude` or `sh -c` wrappers.
- run() now passes `parentPid: resolveClaudeHostPid() ?? process.ppid` — when
  no claude host is found (non-linux, exotic launchers) the legacy direct
  parent is kept, strictly no worse than before.
- tests: injected-proc-table units for the walk (transient sh, zombie wrapper,
  npm install shape, no-match, over-depth) plus a live-tree e2e — a fake
  claude binary launching the hook through `/bin/sh -c` pins both sides of
  the lifetime: the proxy must survive the wrapper's death and must exit with
  the claude session. Verified the e2e fails on the old wiring at exactly the
  "proxy survives" assertion.

test: scope the live-tree claude e2e to linux

CI's test matrix includes windows-latest; the e2e spawns a shebang'ed fake
claude through /bin/sh and relies on the /proc walk (the fix itself falls
back to the legacy parent there, by design). Skip it off-linux, mirroring
the win32-only guards in fix-679-windows-launch.test.ts.

fix: resolve the claude host via ps/powershell where /proc is absent

resolveClaudeHostPid now walks the platform process table: /proc on
linux (fast path, unchanged), `ps -ww -o ppid= -o args=` on darwin/BSD,
and one Get-CimInstance Win32_Process call on windows. Whitespace-
splitting a joined command line can only lose a match (paths with
spaces), never invent one, so a miss still degrades to the legacy
direct-parent fallback — strictly no worse than before.

fix: shared stable-port proxy now outlives its first owner (#7)

Two concurrent claude sessions share one stable-port proxy, but the
parent-gone watchdog watched only the SPAWNING session's host: when it
exited, the shared proxy died under every other live session
(Connection refused mid-session).

- server: the watchdog is now a watcher SET. The spawning hook seeds it
  via BILI_PARENT_PID; attached sessions register their claude host via
  POST /__bili__/watcher. Shutdown fires only when every owner is gone.
  Single-owner proxies keep the historical 'parent-gone (pid N)' reason;
  multi-owner deaths log 'watchers-gone (pids: ...)'.
- server: daemon proxies (no BILI_PARENT_PID) refuse registrations with
  409 — a registration must never arm a lifetime watchdog on a daemon.
- hook: after attaching, register the resolved claude host pid (2s
  timeout, fire-and-forget: failure only degrades to the old
  single-owner watchdog, never blocks session start).
- tests: platform-neutral route contract (400/409/200 + armed proxy
  exits when its keeper dies) and a linux two-session e2e pinning
  'survives the first exit, dies after the last'.

fix: when no claude host resolves, watch the wrapper's parent, not the wrapper

The no-host fallback used the hook's direct parent — which in a real
SessionStart is always the transient /bin/sh -c wrapper, re-arming the
2s self-kill the walk was built to avoid. chooseWatchdogParentPid now
falls back to the wrapper's parent (claude itself in every session,
even when an exotic install form went unrecognized); interactive-shell
parents and unreadable tables keep the legacy direct-parent behavior.
Also documents why the bare-claude node-arg match is safe (bottom-up
walk: the real claude is always nearer) with a lookalike-loses test.

fix: grace window keeps the shared proxy alive for late registrants (#7)

Live regression caught a race the watcher set alone does not close: the
spawner exited 1s after a second session launched, and the first sweep
after its death killed the proxy before the attacher's registration
landed — the second session still went down.

The watchdog now shuts down only after the watcher set has been EMPTY
for WATCHER_IDLE_GRACE_MS (5s). Any registration in the window (late
attacher, resumed session) re-populates the set and cancels the pending
shutdown; an abandoned proxy still disappears within ~7s of its last
owner.

Route test pins the semantics platform-neutrally: keeper1 dies, keeper2
registers 3s later, proxy survives past the grace window, then dies
within ticks+grace after keeper2.

fix: recognize cmd /c and powershell -Command wrappers as transient

claude launches SessionStart hooks via cmd /c on Windows (or PowerShell
elsewhere than sh); the no-host fallback would otherwise arm the 2s
self-kill watchdog on those transient wrappers exactly like the sh -c
case fixed in 3400a7e. /k and interactive shells stay non-transient.

fix: watcher route joins the gated /__bili/ admin family (#7 review)

The watcher route was spelled /__bili__/watcher (double underscore) —
the only such URL in the file. isAdminPath matches startsWith("/__bili/"),
so the route silently skipped the tunnel-header, loopback and
trusted-origin gates. Rename to /__bili/watcher and pin the placement
with regression asserts (x-bili-tunnel and cross-origin POSTs must be
403-rejected by the gate, never reach the route).

Also stop warning on HTTP 409 from watcher registration: that is the
daemon refusal — a proxy with no watchdog already outlives every
session, nothing to register and nothing to warn about.

fix: guard the CLI entry against host-process imports

opencode 1.18.x's npm plugin loader imports exports["."] (dist/index.js)
into its own process; the unguarded main() then dispatched a CLI against
the HOST's argv — plain `opencode` defaulted to start and died on the
occupied 8787 port, `opencode run x` hit unknown-command and
process.exit(2)'d the host. Only dispatch when this file itself is the
invoked script (realpath(argv[1]) === realpath(import.meta.url); same
posture as the claude-native-bootstrap entry guard).

fix: drain in-flight persist writes before T7 teardown deletes store dir (#1194)

T7's post-turn persist flush (debounceMs 0) fires an async fire-and-forget
write chain; cancelAll() only clears not-yet-fired debounces and never
drains in-flight chains, so rmSync(root) raced the writer and threw
ENOTEMPTY on slow CI runners, killing the v0.1.140 release gate.

Teardown now awaits flushAll() (drains pending AND in-flight chains,
never rejects) before cancelAll(), and rmSync gains maxRetries/retryDelay
as belt-and-braces. Test-only change; zero production code touched.

Closes #1194

feat: image pre-compression for screenshot-heavy tool results (#1095)

Opt-in compress.imageCompression.* (default off): screenshot-like images in
tool results are downscaled once at arrival via the acp-kernel >= 0.0.84
image-compression API (decideImageRoute routing + billing-aware
estimateImageTokens); the host executes the encode with an optional sharp
dependency (lazy-loaded; missing or failing => original passes through,
never blocking the main flow). All four wire carriers are rewritten at the
forward boundary: anthropic image blocks, openai image_url parts (including
single-string data-URL messages; remote URLs untouched), responses input_image,
and google inlineData. Non-screenshot images pass through byte-identical.

Lossy-by-nature backstops: originals cached in memory (64 MB cap, FIFO) and an
injected image_full tool restoring the original resolution for the rest of the
session when the model can't read details (sticky, idempotent; shrink records
and restore state persist across restarts in session state). Per-image savings
log as [acp-image] lines and aggregate into the [acp-usage] suffix
(img-saved=Ntok/MKB xK). A double-shrink guard keeps the substituted-at-arrival
bytes as the standing wire content (prefix-cache invariant, same contract as
CCR #1097): a ref with existing shrink records only accepts payloads matching
its known original fingerprints.

Disabled (the default) means byte-identical pass-through and no image_full on
the wire. New optional dependency: sharp ^0.35.4 (optionalDependencies; a
failed install degrades to pass-through). Tests: tests/image-compress.test.ts

fix(build): keep optional native dep sharp external in tsup bundle

tsup does not auto-externalize optionalDependencies, so without an explicit
entry the native sharp module would be inlined into dist/index.js — breaking
both the lazy-import fallback (missing sharp must degrade to pass-through)
and build reproducibility (the caret range would bake a resolved version
into the bundle). Verified: built dist/index.js contains exactly one
lazy import("sharp") and no bundled sharp code.

prepareAnthropic/Google/Responses all append the ephemeral imageFullTrailingNote

pattern as the other three wires: trailing user message only, never in the

refactor: drop unused imageOriginals cache — restore rides client history

imageOriginals (64 MB FIFO) was write-only: executeImageFull never reads it.
Restore is passive — the kernel marks the ref restored and the client's own
history still carries the original bytes (it never saw the shrunk form), so
originals ride the wire again without any proxy-side storage. Removing the
dead cache also removes its per-session memory ceiling. Typecheck confirms no

docs: correct image-compression restore mechanics and post-restart behavior

The docs described a proxy-side in-memory originals cache (64 MB FIFO) as

after restart. Neither is true: restore needs no proxy storage (client
history carries the originals), and after a restart previously-shrunk
unrestored refs pass through at original resolution until session reset while

fix: break logger EPIPE feedback loop — async stderr error re-enters uncaughtException (#1233)

On Linux, stderr over a pipe is an async stream: EPIPE surfaces as an 'error' event, not a sync throw, so the try/catch around process.stderr.write() never saw it. - logger.ts: module-init 'error' listener on process.stderr flips logging to file-only once (single [warn]); sync write failures (Windows) take the same path; log() skips stderr after the flip so the logger's error path never re-enters the writer that produced the error.
- server.ts: uncaughtException handler logs the first stream-write error and suppresses repeats (belt-and-suspenders for non-logger writers).
- tests/logger-epipe.test.ts: spawn-based regression (closed stderr pipe -> no storm, durable record intact, exactly one warn) + predicate unit test. Red on unpatched code, green with the fix.

fix: GC the CCR content-store companions (#1180)

Session-file GC (#1082) ignored the per-session CCR content stores added
by #1097: walkSessionFiles picked up <hash>.content-store.json but
viewFromParsed rejected it (no savedAt field), so it was counted
unreadable and kept forever — and when a session file WAS deleted its
sibling store was never unlinked, orphaning potentially large lossless
payload files with no code path to clean them.

- co-delete the companion when its session file is deleted
- sweep orphaned companions (session file already gone) once past the
  age gate; the reference check matches the shared hash stem across
  namespaces (meta fill-once can migrate _unknown/ -> namespaced
  without cleaning the old path), so a live store is never
  false-orphaned across that move
- fold the store footprint (unique-content chars / 4) into the
  maxTokens gate: a tiny session carrying a huge store no longer slips
  under the size ceiling
- unreadable/foreign companion next to an otherwise-eligible session
  keeps both files (never guess at unreadable data)
- per-file audit lines for companion deletions (path + size), plus a
  companionsRemoved counter in GcResult (removed stays session files)
- docs: companion lifecycle noted in README + CONFIGURATION, en/zh

fix: keep live fallback content stores when GC deletes a stale namespace duplicate (#1180)

Meta fill-once (session.ts getSession) migrates a session _unknown/<h>.json -> ns/host_<h>.json without cleaning the old path (kernel StateStore writes never delete the previous relPath), and saveContentStore only rewrites when dirty. A moved CCR session whose store was not re-saved since the move therefore still reads its LIVE store from the stale duplicate's sibling (loadContentStore probes _unknown/ when the namespaced store is absent, stopping at the first existing candidate). The co-delete pairing is strictly same-directory, so sweeping the aged duplicate would unlink live lossless payload bytes.

Guard: skip the companion unlink when another surviving session file shares the hash stem and has no store of its own. The bytes then stay referenced until that twin itself is swept, after which the orphan pass collects them. When the twin owns its own (shadowing) store the flat sibling is dead bytes and co-deletion proceeds as before.

Adds 3 regression tests: duplicate + fresh twin without own store (store kept); duplicate + twin with own store (dead copy co-deleted, live one kept); both copies eligible (whole session incl. lone store swept, order-independent).

fix: count all post-fold requests in cache ledger turnsToNextFold

(f.at <= s.at); the consumedFoldSeq gate remains on the pending list only,
so compRepay/T attribution semantics are unchanged. With counting fixed, the
existing pushFold freeze of k = requestsAfter becomes exactly the batch-path
turnsToNextFold window under chronological sample arrival — no new persistent
field, no ledger format change.

A native hook attaches to whatever answers on the port. A manually started
'bili start' daemon has no lifecycle owner (refuses watcher registration,
never dies with its sessions, often runs an older bili build) — attaching to
it is how #1322 happened.

auto-discovery lane inherits it once: claude-native, kimi, dsh, omp, opencode

its health endpoint reports an armed session-lifecycle watchdog

currently installed bili.

state. Explicit user-directed attaches (kimi/dsh BILLION_CONTEXT_ATTACH /
preset BILLION_CONTEXT_PROXY) bypass discovery entirely and stay exempt.

feat: bili acp-cache diff — prefix-diff attribution over ACP_DUMP_BODY dumps (#1266)

New read-only diagnostic command 'bili acp-cache diff <dump-dir>': pairs
adjacent same-session requests from ACP_DUMP_BODY dumps (INCOMING = client
wire, REQ = proxy-rebuilt wire) and classifies each pair:

- pure-append         prefix stable, growth only at the tail (healthy)
- mid-stream-rewrite  first divergent byte inside the shared prefix; reports
                      byte offset + first divergent message and attributes
                      proxy vs client vs both by comparing where each side's
                      wire first diverged (#1249 shape = incoming append +
                      outgoing mid drift -> proxy)
- prefix-stable-miss  outgoing prefix append but provider usage shows the
                      cached prefix collapsed (--log / bili.log correlation;
                      upstream TTL/eviction, the unattributed bucket of
                      acp-kernel#393)

Comparison is two-tier: byte-prefix first, then JSON message-array-aware so
a healthy array append (which moves the closing bracket) is not misread as a
mid-stream rewrite. Output: per-pair lines + worst offenders; --json emits
the machine-readable report. --log FILE / --no-log control usage-log
correlation (default auto-discovers <dump-dir>/bili.log or defaultLogFile()).

Prerequisite fix in the same issue scope: INCOMING dump filenames now carry
the bound session id (<ts>-<sid>-INCOMING.txt; OUTGOING already had it) so
concurrent sessions can be paired; the dump moves from the pre-prepare site
to right after prepare, where the session is bound. Requests rejected before
prepare no longer get an INCOMING dump (they never got a REQ dump either);
legacy session-less INCOMING dumps still parse via timestamp proximity.

Tests: synthetic dump pairs for all three shapes + legacy filenames + usage
alignment + render modes (tests/acp-cache-diff.test.ts), parseArgs cases,
and a full-proxy harness test pinning the new INCOMING filename.

fix: hold dsh first model request until ACP tool registration (#1268)

A fresh dsh native session fires its first model request as soon as the
proxy origin is ready, but ACP manifest registration lands ~90ms later
(proxy spawn dominates boot). The first request then short-circuits at
headersFor (!toolsReady) and rides wire mode un-stamped — the #1158
'zero proxy traffic silently unclaimed' failure class, deterministic for
single-shot headless invocations where the whole session is round one.

Add an optional toolsReady gate to NativeInterceptState: model-API
requests await it (bounded by readyTimeoutMs) before headersFor is
consulted, in both the routed (/bili/) and main rewrite paths. Only the
dsh lane arms it (apply() resolves it when the first registration attempt
finishes, success or failure); every other lane leaves it undefined and
is behaviorally unchanged. Timeout or failed registration falls through
to exactly today's wire-mode behavior; a later maybeRetry success flips
stamping on without re-arming.

fix(ccr): give plugin-mode retrieve delivery a lifecycle so acks can't outlive lost text

In plugin mode, acp_retrieve committed its success (ack text + retrieveHits)
before the full text had any guaranteed delivery path: the ack rode the tool
response immediately while the full text sat in the volatile in-memory
session.pendingRetrievals queue, appended only to a LATER upstream request. A
restart, an upstream failure after drain, a CCR disarm, or a long run of
non-qualifying requests could each leave the ack on record while the text was
silently lost or surfaced detached from context.

Give queued retrievals a lifecycle (queued -> attached -> delivered | dropped):
- executeRetrieve queues with a durable undelivered ledger in session.metadata
  (round-trips to disk; no on-disk schema change).
- Plugin-lane prepares SNAPSHOT (not splice) the queue onto the outgoing body;
  forward() settles it at the final response: committed on 2xx, dropped-and-
  logged on network failure / non-2xx / transform failure.
- Disarm terminates pending deliveries observably (no silent truncate, no stale
  flush on re-arm); reload reconciles acked-but-never-delivered refs; a TTL
  (BILI_CCR_RETRIEVAL_TTL_MS, default 10min) expires loudly.
- Every loss logs refs+count+reason, bumps stats.retrieveDropped, and queues a
  corrective note flushed as an ephemeral trailing user message next round.
- New additive counter stats.retrieveDelivered counts confirmed deliveries.
  retrieveHits semantics are unchanged.

Range-restore riders (#1207) share the carrier but are ccr:false: removed at
the delivery outcome but exempt from the CCR ledger/TTL/counters/note, so their
original ride-along semantics are preserved. Proxy-mode drain is unchanged
(atomic in-flow) -- four-wire happy path and pair integrity intact.

Tests cover all four windows plus two-riders isolation and the proxy regression.

fix: never spawn a second instance over a model channel pinned to an unreachable attach target (#1365)

When a dsh/opencode attach target (BILLION_CONTEXT_PROXY) is transiently unreachable, the old verifyAttachAndRecover unconditionally fell back to spawning a second proxy instance. If the process's provider baseURL statically routes model traffic through that target (/bili/<upstream>), the model channel stays pinned to the original origin while bili tools move to the spawned one — every tool call then 404s 'unknown plugin conversation', the context can no longer be compressed, and preflight fails with 502 until the session is abandoned.

Fix: observe routed-channel evidence (state.routedOrigin, recorded by the shared fetch patch and the opencode V2 route before any gate await). With evidence, a dead attach target is WAITED ON (BILI_ATTACH_HEALTH_DEADLINE_MS, default 15s) instead of migrated away from; on timeout the failure is loud and self-healing (register base cleared, re-probed on every model request, ~10s cadence) and the env stays frozen. Without evidence, a grace window (BILI_ATTACH_EVIDENCE_GRACE_MS, default 5s) covers the decision-before-first-request race; expiry keeps the legacy #983/#1130 spawn fallback byte-for-byte. Late evidence rebinds the tool channel to where the models actually go (convergence rule).

Stacked on PR #1275 (toolsReady gate); rebases onto master once that lands. Closes #1365

whose path needs them (e.g. "C:\Users\...\claude.exe"). The basename + flag
matching in isClaudeHostArgv / isTransientShArgv saw a trailing quote
(claude.exe") and missed BOTH the claude host and the transient sh wrapper,
so resolveClaudeHostPid returned undefined, the fallback also missed, and the
watchdog watched the dying wrapper bash -> parent-gone -> ~8s self-kill on
every Windows session. Quoted variant of #1182; #1185 fixed Linux only.

Fix: stripQuotes() peels leading/trailing quote chars before basename/flag
matching in both functions (all three flag branches). A no-op for already-clean
inputs (Unix NUL-split /proc argv, macOS ps), so Linux/macOS behavior is
unchanged. readWinProcInfo still returns raw tokens; stripping is a matching
concern.

Tests: tests/cross-platform-argv.test.ts (8) pin quoted AND clean argv shapes
resolving identically across all three layers (matcher / walk / decision), plus
false-positive guards (hook's own script, lookalikes, empty names stay rejected).

(gated); build success. Regression repro (user's exact quoted chain): before

fix: targeted no-re-issue receipt for content-less compress calls (#1366)

A compress call carrying no content at all ({} / empty-string args — observed in #1366 as an 'empty companion' compress() emitted alongside the valid one) got the generic format lecture ending in 'Re-issue the compress call'. A structurally empty call can never satisfy that instruction, so a weak FC model looped the identical spec until the #847 repeat-failure guard tripped (~2h of context burn in the incident).

applyRanges now detects the truly-empty case (kind empty-input / missing-content without per-entry reasons, excluding the #362 {ranges: ...} shape drift where re-issue IS the right advice) and returns a receipt that names the actual defect and forbids the re-issue. The #847 guard still records these failures; every other receipt is byte-identical.

fix: hedge the span-hint covered-prefix claim — gaps below the boundary stay compressible (#1366)

compressibleSpanHint told models '(everything up to mNNNNN is already inside active blocks)'. Blocks need not be contiguous: in the #1366 session a live gap (m05027–m05052 between two active blocks) sat below the boundary, and the flat claim contributed to the model's 'nudge vs tool conflict' confusion. Wording now hedges ('largely inside ... isolated free gaps may still exist'); kernel validation was always authoritative. Labeled in-passing fix found while working #1366.

fix: derived pi sessions inherit parent blocks via read-only fallback (#1333)

A pi RLM inline spawn (PI_ACP_FORK_HOST=1) starts as a fresh conversation
with zero compression state: decompress/search_context could not serve
anything its parent had folded. The child's pi session header names its
parent (parentSession path), so the plugin now reports the derivation at
register (parentConversationId on both identity and pending channels) and
the proxy records the link on the child's first request
(metadata.derivedFromSessionId, resolved through the conversation map).

No state is copied. The kernel's syncBlocks deactivates blocks whose
source messages are absent from the incoming wire, so seeding a child
that never resends its parent's history never sticks — instead
decompress and search_context fall back to the parent chain at read
time: read-only, cycle-guarded, depth cap 8, parent untouched.

fix: emit SessionStart hook commands that survive every client shell

The SessionStart hook is the one place bili hands a client a SHELL STRING
rather than an argv array, so the client's own shell re-parses our path.
Two Windows shapes break it, both hit in the field on Claude Code 2.1.282:

1. Backslashes are escape-eaten by POSIX shells. `D:\Dev\node\node.exe`
   loses `\D` and `\n` and becomes `D:Devnodenode.exe` — command not found.
   The hook never starts the proxy while the client's base_url already
   points at the fixed port, so the session HANGS on a dead origin instead
   of failing loudly. Forward slashes are accepted by every shell we emit
   for, so the fix is to forward-slash both the exe and its arguments.

2. Quoting the COMMAND token is not portable:

        form                    bash   PowerShell          cmd
        bare token               ok       ok               ok
        "quoted" first token     ok     PARSE ERR *       ok
        & "quoted" first token  ERR       ok              ERR

   *PowerShell reads a leading quoted token as a STRING EXPRESSION: with an
   argument after it the whole command dies at parse time (`UnexpectedToken`,
   taking the hook command with it) and on its own it exits 0 having run
   nothing — a silent no-op, worse than an error.

   No spelling covers a spaced command path in all three shells, so the only
   question is which shell to keep working. Windows runs Claude Code's
   SessionStart hooks through PowerShell — probe-verified: a cmd-only builtin
   (`ver > file`) writes nothing while a PowerShell-only one
   (`Write-Output ... > file`) writes its file, and a bash shell would have
   created an EMPTY file rather than a populated one. So `&` is the form that
   keeps the real hook path alive. cmd never sees a spaced command here: the
   kimi hook resolves a bare `node` through PATH and so is never quoted.

Quoting an ARGUMENT is safe in all three shells and is kept for paths that
need it (a spaced temp dir or username is the common case).

Both call sites now share `portableHookCommand(exe, args)` — claude
(`process.execPath` + the bootstrap script) and kimi (`node` + the hook
script, previously built with `path.join`, which is the same bug via
backslashes).

Tests: tests/hook-command.test.ts pins the exact spelling AND runs the
produced command through every shell the platform actually has, so a fix that
only looks right on paper fails. tests/kimi-native.test.ts asserted
`endsWith(path.join(...))`, which pinned the backslash bug — it now asserts
the portable shape.

Full suite: 2659 tests, 2640 pass. The 11 failures are pre-existing on a
clean tree (identical names and counts).

test: pin uninstall-detection regex against every emitted hook form (#1376)

isOursSessionStartEntry is how bili recognizes its own SessionStart hook on
uninstall/reinstall. The portable emitter can now produce a quoted trailing

fix: refresh a stale SessionStart hook command on reinstall (#1376)

applyClaudeManagedBlock appended our SessionStart entry only when no bili
entry was present, so a settings file written by an older release kept its
old command forever. The old command is exactly what #1376 fixes, and its
failure mode is a silent hang — no log, no error — so an affected install
had no way to learn it needed a manual remove + reinstall.

Reinstall now rewrites any command we own whose text differs from the one
this build emits, matching what the same function already does for
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. A user entry is never touched, and a second apply with
the same command still changes nothing.

notes.length === 0 for a changed hook command, pinning the skip-if-present
behaviour; it now asserts the rewrite. A new case covers the field shape —
a 0.1.153 Windows command with backslashes and JSON.stringify quotes.

fix: stop leaking prompt_cache_key into anthropic upstreams (#1403)

The omp extension stamped a raw session UUID as top-level
prompt_cache_key on every chat-shaped payload regardless of where it
was headed. Strict-schema upstreams behind a blind TLS tunnel (e.g.
opencode zen's /v1/messages) reject unknown fields with 400 "Extra
inputs are not permitted" — 100% failure for every anthropic-protocol
model through `bili omp`.

Producer fix (src/agent): stampPromptCacheKey now stamps only when the
destination will actually reach the proxy's processing pipeline
(proxyBaseFromUrl / BILLION_CONTEXT_PROXY origin / BILI_MITM_HOSTS
membership). The pck stamp is load-bearing identity (#268) but is
useless — and harmful — for hosts the proxy cannot see.

Defense in depth (src/server): scrubAnthropicPck strips the field from
anthropic bodies on every verbatim forward path (side request #388,
chain verdict #1086, passthrough marks #1117/#920, non-conversation
relay #1284, final fallback covering --passthrough and route
passthrough #661). Bodies without the field stay byte-identical;
openai/responses wires are untouched (dsh native pck forwarding intact).

Launcher exports BILI_MITM_HOSTS to pi/omp children so the extension
sees exactly the proxy's MITM whitelist.

Wire-contract ledger: WC-007 records that top-level prompt_cache_key
is not part of the Anthropic Messages API (provenance: #1403).

Behavior changes (old -> new):
- omp pck stamping: unconditional -> destination-gated. Blind-tunneled
  destinations lose pck identity (anonymous prefix-affinity sessions,
  #309) instead of corrupting the upstream request with a foreign
  field.
- Verbatim anthropic forwards: client bytes verbatim including any
  top-level prompt_cache_key -> field stripped (re-serialization only
  when present). The #661 byte-for-byte guarantee now applies to
  pck-free bodies (the normal case).
- New additive env var BILI_MITM_HOSTS exported to pi/omp children.

Tests: new tests/anthropic-pck-verbatim.test.ts (strict-upstream A/B
for all four leak paths), route-passthrough assertions updated to
semantic strip checks plus a byte-exact no-pck test, plugin-agent
matrix extended with destination-gate cases, WC-007 self-check probe.
Full suite green (2800 tests / 0 fail), typecheck clean, build OK,
e2e zero-token preflight pass.

Closes #1403

The corrective note for a failed retrieve delivery was destructively consumed at prepare time (flushRetrievalNotes deleted metadata.ccrDropNotes before the upstream outcome was known). Notes now carry a stable id (randomUUID, persisted in session metadata) and follow snapshot -> attach -> commit: prepare* snapshots non-destructively and records the ids on Prepared; forward() commits them only when the final upstream response is 2xx. The rendered text is byte-identical to before; retrieveDelivered/retrieveDropped semantics are unchanged; pre-fix persisted no-id notes normalize to "" and clear on first confirmed delivery; the buffer is capped at 64 (oldest evicted first).

UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT was classified upstream-timeout and never retried, so a single ~10s connect failure during a proxy-tool re-request killed the whole turn (#1453). It is now its own kind: the TCP handshake provably never completed, nothing reached the upstream, and each attempt costs at most one connect timeout — bounded, unlike the headers/body idle budget it was lumped with. ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN (dns) join the fail-fast set for the same pre-response reason.

fix: end re-request transport failures in-band with a committed-work note (#1453)

A non-HTTP error from the post-compress re-request escaped runCompressLoop and surfaced as a bare 'fetch failed' stream error — even though the round's compression had already landed. Client abort keeps the throwing path.
