fix: surface parse-dropped compress entries; normalize single-object content (#1494)

Two param-shape defects in the proxy compress path:

1. Silent partial failure: entries a batched compress call contained that
   the kernel parser rejected (bad bounds, missing summary, broken JSON
   fragment) vanished from the receipt — 'Compressed A, B → 2 block(s)'
   with no note about the dropped entry and no server log line (the warn
   only fired when ALL entries failed). Models believed the fold landed
   and never re-issued the lost range.

2. Asymmetric shape tolerance: retrying the lost range with content given
   as the single entry object (or a bare top-level array / string-encoded
   variants) hit kernel kind=content-not-array/not-object — a hard failure
   on shapes the kernel's salvage ladder already accepts at the top level.

Fixes:
- normalizeCompressInput (src/compress-tool.ts): wrap single-object content
  in a one-element array, bare top-level arrays into {content:[…]}, and
  recover the same shapes from string-encoded args (fenced / double-
  stringified). Canonical inputs pass through byte-identical.
- applyRanges (src/stream.ts): append a model-facing REJECTED note with the
  kernel per-entry reasons to BOTH the success receipt and the 0-blocks
  failure message; log server-side ('compress PARTIAL').
- parseCompressInput: warn-log partial drops (previously invisible because
  diagnostics.ok was true whenever ≥1 range survived).

Behavior changes (disclosed):
- Previously hard-failing param shapes are now accepted (single-object
  content, bare array, their string-encoded variants): old = full call
  failure, new = normalized fold.
- Tool receipts gain an optional extra line on partial drops: old = silent
  under-reporting, new = explicit rejection note + re-issue guidance.
- Garbage object content now reports kind=no-valid-ranges with per-entry
  reasons instead of opaque content-not-array (still a failure).

fix: gate stale estimate baselines out of nudge/preflight sizing (#1492)

After an upstream failure without a usage report, armFailureShrink raises
stats.lastInputTokens (source=estimate) to chars/4 of the body just sent. On
kernel-transform-failure fallbacks that body is the UNFOLDED raw client
history, so the poisoned baseline survives across turns while upstream keeps
failing and three source-blind consumers apply it cross-turn:

- effectiveTokenCount fed it to decideNudge -> false emergency bands
- preflight trigger max()'d it against the post-fold payload estimate
- the preflight loop floor pinned currentTokens at the stale value, burning
  summarization rounds over a payload whose own estimate fits the window

Rule now: an estimate-sourced baseline may floor sizing decisions only while
the current payload is unmeasurable (processedMessages empty). Usage-sourced
baselines keep flooring everywhere. armFailureShrink also measures with
defaultCountTokens (CJK-aware lower bound) instead of estimateTokensFast
(chars/4); ASCII output is byte-identical.

feat: BILI_STREAM_STALL_MS streaming-phase stall guard (#1452)

Opt-in guard for upstream streams that go silent AFTER the first body
byte: BILI_STREAM_STALL_MS=<ms> arms a per-request timer that resets on
every chunk; expiry aborts the fetch with a DOMException AbortError whose
message names the budget and #1452. The abort flows through the existing
#721 in-band truncation chain (upstream_stream_truncated frame + [DONE]
+ clean FIN) — same wire outcome as an upstream that FINs mid-stream,
just detected after N ms of silence instead of waiting for the client to
give up. Default 0 = off: behavior is byte-identical when unset.

fix: drain-then-close on clientError + connection lifecycle ledger, kat knob, exposure telemetry (#1452)

clientError: Node's default disposition (no listener) destroys the socket;
with residual bytes in the kernel recv buffer the OS then answers RST
(the #1452 incident signature) or strands the peer's pooled connection
with neither FIN nor RST. The handler drains then end()s — clean FIN in
every case — with a warn marker. One handler covers plain TCP and MITM
TLS legs alike (same server instance).

Lifecycle ledger: every accepted socket gets a ConnRecord (kind, request
count, last-response-end); on close it logs one debug line classifying
the initiator — peer-fin / idle-timeout / server-end / error(code) /
destroyed — so the next RST incident can be adjudicated from logs alone.
End markers use performance.now() (µs): same-millisecond closes are the
norm (the FIN receiver reacts immediately), only sub-ms resolution keeps
causal order. idle-timeout keys off the response budget because Node's
keep-alive reaper destroy()s idle sockets without prefinish/end.

keepAliveTimeout: was an implicit Node default (5s); now explicit 5000ms,
configurable via BILI_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS (default unchanged), logged
at startup.

Exposure telemetry: one info line per BILI_EXPOSURE_LOG_INTERVAL_MS
(default hourly, 0 disables) with liveConns/tcpHandles/handles/sessions/
blindTunnels/inFlight — ground truth for long-process fd/connection drift
(both #1452 incidents died inside one 36.7h process). blindTunnels comes
from a new liveBlindTunnels() counter in mitm.ts (incremented on tunnel
establish, decremented once on first leg close).

Shutdown force-exit warning gains (liveConns=N). All new lines are
debug/info/warn-level diagnostics or default-invariant config.

fix: accept SSH-forwarded local port in admin origin gate (#1537)

The management-endpoint origin check pinned Host/Origin to the actual listen port (req.socket.localPort), so a Web UI reached through 'ssh -L <local>:127.0.0.1:<remote>' was rejected with 403 because the browser presents the local forward port, not the remote listen port.

feat: terminal backstop for the clientError drain path (#1529)

#1452 item 1 replaced the clientError socket destroy with drain-then-close

review: if the peer NEVER sends FIN after the bail (adversarial /
slowloris-style: parse-garbage then silence), the socket stays half-open on
our side indefinitely — the keep-alive reaper keys off completed responses
and Node enables no SO_KEEPALIVE by default. Each such socket holds a
connRecords ledger entry plus kernel buffers.

timer for BILI_CLIENT_ERROR_BACKSTOP_MS (default 30000; 0 restores the
hold-until-peer-death status quo; non-numeric/negative fall back). On fire,
if the socket is still alive and the peer FIN never arrived, destroy it.

- Distinct ledger reason clienterror-backstop (checked first so a racing

  listeners or timers (drainArmed guard on ConnRecord).
- Behavior change: old = half-open clientError sockets held until peer
  death; new = destroyed ~300ms + 30s after clientError unless the peer
  FINs first. The common case is byte-for-byte unchanged (well-behaved
  peers FIN within ms of our drain-FIN and get the clean FIN as before).
- Config surface: one new env var, documented in CONFIGURATION.md en+zh.

fix: keep in-place summary in post-fold re-request view (#1548)

refreshFolded rebuilt the round-2 re-request by mixing the ephemeral
acp_loop_* tool pair into the message list BEFORE stripKernelSummaries
judged carrier presence — so the proxy's own ephemeral compress call made
it drop the in-place acp_summary for exactly one request. Proxy-mode
clients never echo that pair (adapters buffer-to-finish), so the next
client turn re-inserted the summary at the fold anchor and the upstream
longest-prefix match collapsed to the stable head: observed production
floor of a constant ~16.5K cached tokens after every fold instead of
~95%.

Strip against inbound-derived messages only: when the compress call rides
inbound history (plugin-mode agent persisting its own carrier) behavior is
unchanged; when it exists only as an ephemeral loop record the in-place
summary survives, so round-2 and the next client turn share bytes through
the fold anchor and the cacheable region extends past the fold.

Regression test drives a codex-shaped Responses session through the real
proxy and pins: summary present in round-2, byte-identical prefix through
the anchor on the next turn, append-stability during plain growth.

fix: position-preserve mid-history system/developer items on the plugin responses lane (#1638)

OMP-style plugin clients append custom_message-derived developer
notifications mid-history and re-send them every turn. The kernel's
responsesToCore hoists system/developer content from ANY position into
projection.systemParts, and prepareResponses re-injects the merged block
at input[0] — so every notification append rewrote the outbound FIRST
item and the upstream prefix cache missed the whole input (production
sawtooth: cached pinned to the instructions-only residual, #1638).

In plugin mode, mark the non-head system/developer items with an
unknown type just for the duration of responsesToCore: they land in the
projection layout as coreId-less slots and patchResponsesInput re-emits
them verbatim in their original position — the position-preserved
semantics the openai-chat wire already has (head-only hoist). The head
run keeps the hoist (stable system prompt), so the front developer
block stays byte-identical across turns. Proxy mode (native codex)
keeps the hoist-and-anchor behavior (#1085) untouched.

Transition cost: one-time cache miss per active plugin session at
upgrade (front block no longer carries accumulated notification text).

byte-stability + in-place notification re-emission + append-only bodies
+ no sentinel leak; fold interaction (in-place carrier counts keep the
#1567 pins); leading additional_tools head-neutrality; proxy-mode
negative pin (hoist semantics unchanged). Fills the developer-item gap
neptune62 flagged in #1650/#1663.

test: scope abort-seam stall detection to abort phases only (#1651)

send() applied a 250ms per-read deadline to every turn, so environmental read gaps on loaded runners misclassified completion-path turns as aborted ('aborted' !== 'ok', CI run 36522935472, windows-latest cell). The per-read race now runs only when the caller opts in via send(STALL_DETECT_MS) - the two intentional abort phases. fix: hold SSE clients across streaming silence past undici's 300s body timeout (#1647)

After the 2xx commit, bili's rewrite/strip pipes swallow upstream SSE
comment pings and buffer whole rounds before emitting anything, so a
prefill longer than 300s writes zero bytes to the client and the
client-side undici default bodyTimeout kills the connection (leg 2 was
already protected by #551/#556; this is leg 1). Wrappers then misread
the death as a dead proxy and silently re-send the request DIRECT,
losing compression and cancelling the in-flight GPU prefill.

- beginStreamKeepalive(): sibling of the #568 preflight hold. Armed once
  per response at the 2xx commit point for SSE responses; while zero
  bytes reach the socket it emits one SSE comment line
  (`: bili-keepalive`, a spec-level no-op). Tracks socket-level
  bytesWritten so any downstream writer (plugin pipe, compress loop, raw
  passthrough) resets the clock; self-clears on res close, so no stop()
  threading through the pipe branches.
- New env BILI_STREAM_KEEPALIVE_MS (default 15000, live-read at arm
  time, 0 disables), documented in CONFIGURATION.md / .zh-CN.md next to
  BILI_PREFLIGHT_HOLD_MS.
- Client-disconnect-mid-stream log now reports elapsed time + bytes
  written to client, separating an undici-timeout kill from a user cancel.
- tests/stream-keepalive.test.ts: slow-upstream case asserts keepalive
  comments arrive while upstream pings stay swallowed AND the stream
  completes intact; fast stream gets zero injected bytes; 0 disables.

Closes #1647

fix: /bili/ tunnel admission treats DNS failure as transport-class (502) with bounded retry (#1686)

A transiently unreachable DNS server made checkTunnelDestination's single
admission lookup fail, which the server answered with HTTP 403
(tunnel_destination_denied). Clients read 403 as a permanent permission
denial, killed their retry logic, and the agent workflow died — while the
same domain forwarded fine seconds later once the resolver recovered.

- tunnel-guard: bound the admission lookup to 3 attempts with 250ms backoff
  and a 2s per-attempt timeout (race; @types/node lacks lookup({timeout})).
  A transient blip now rides out inside the retry window.
- tunnel-guard: malformed embedded URLs get their own verdict code 'invalid'
  so they are no longer conflated with resolution failure.
- server: verdict → status split: policy denials (self/linkLocal/privateRemote)
  stay 403; 'unresolvable' becomes 502 (transport-class, retryable); 'invalid'
  becomes 400 (client error).

Behavior change (disclosed): for /bili/ absolute-URL requests whose destination
cannot be resolved, the response status changes 403 -> 502 (body shape
unchanged). Malformed embedded URLs: 403 -> 400. Admission latency under a
sustained outage is now bounded (~6.5s worst case) instead of hanging for the
OS resolver's full timeout (tens of seconds on Windows).

fix(#1691): honor decompress toFile destination (was ignored -> os.tmpdir())

The decompress tool advertised a toFile argument in its schema and prompt but never read it: every restore went to os.tmpdir() above 10K chars and inlined below, silently discarding any caller-supplied path. resolveDecompress (single chokepoint for the whole-block and CCR range paths) now routes through a shared toFilePointer helper: an explicit non-empty string destination wins regardless of body size, resolves relative paths against the proxy cwd, creates parent dirs, writes 0600, and returns/queues only a lean pointer (never inflating context). Explicit paths are intentionally left out of the temp-file reaper. Absent/empty toFile falls back to the prior behavior byte-for-byte; malformed (non-string) values log a one-line warning.

fix(#1647): keep-alive comments only at SSE line boundaries

Every processed pipe in server.ts (compress-loop rewriter, plugin strip
pipes, buffered fake-completion rounds) re-emits whole events, so the
injection point was already boundary-safe by construction. But the
arming gate (prepared?.stream === true && upstream SSE) does NOT exclude
every raw forwarder: reasoning-guard.ts's JSON-parse-failure passthrough
pipes upstream chunks verbatim (pipeThroughRaw res.write(value)) on a
lane where the keep-alive is armed. An upstream that flushes a partial
data: line and then stalls would get the comment spliced into the
client's JSON.

Guard: observe the last byte written to res (chain-wrap res.write once,
mirroring the #806 watchdog patch) and skip the beat while mid-line; the
300s budget tolerates skips, corruption does not. State lives on the res
object so a second arming shares one truth. Adds a unit test that pins
the invariant: partial line + stall => zero comments; line completes =>
keep-alive resumes at the boundary only. Also documents the ≈2x
effective cadence (a keep-alive write itself counts as progress).

Test-only export: beginStreamKeepalive.

body-markers; now neither unless opted in. Header-based chains unchanged.

fix: classify opencode v2 title-gen by host-declared intent, not token budget (#1699)

opencode v2 sends title-gen requests with NO max_tokens (options {} for
kind==="title"), so bili's isTitleGen / side-request heuristic — which defaults
a missing output budget to 8192 — misclassified them as main turns and injected
the full ~11KiB compress philosophy prompt + ACP compress tool into the title
model. Result: garbage session titles (English chat sentence / empty first line).

Forward the host's per-request persona id on a new x-bili-plugin-agent header
(stamped by the opencode v2 plugin from its own request scope) and treat a known
side-request agent ("title") as a side request BY INTENT, routing it verbatim
(no injection, kernel state untouched) regardless of output budget. Main personas
(build/plan/general) are deliberately absent from the set, so real turns keep
compression. The header reader is gated on plugin announcement so a plain client
cannot declare a side request by name to dodge compression.

Behavior change (intended): an opencode v2 title-gen request WITHOUT max_tokens
now routes verbatim instead of being treated as a main turn. Previously it got
the full compress philosophy prompt + tool injected; now it does not. This only
affects requests that carry x-bili-plugin-agent: title; every other request is
untouched.

fix: keep prose between paired render tags in tag-echo filter (#1720)

The PAIRED regex's inner group ([^<>]{0,64}) was meant to hold a tag ref
but matched any up-to-64 non-angle-bracket characters, including newlines
and ordinary assistant prose; stripAcpTags then deleted the whole match,
silently eating answer text that happened to sit between a leaked open and
close tag. The streaming filter had the same hole via its LONE_OPEN ->
swallow-until-close path for spans within the swallow budget.

Narrow PAIRED to a real ref shape (m + >=4 digits, optional surrounding
whitespace) and make the streaming swallow release a non-ref body at close
time, dropping only the tag fragments. Ref echoes are still stripped
completely on both paths; imitation swallowing is unchanged.

The main forward hop was the only request path still doing a single attempt:
one millisecond DNS/reset/refused/connect-timeout blip killed the whole round
(502 'acp-proxy failure') while acp-loop/preflight/compress loops already
replayed under fetchWithRetry (#1263/#189).

- fetch-util: new fetchWithTransportRetry — replays ONLY pre-response
  fail-fast network deaths (isFailFastUpstreamKind) under the existing
  BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX / BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_BASE_MS budget; any HTTP verdict
  (ok/4xx/5xx) passes through untouched. fetchWithRetry itself is unsuitable
  here: it also retries transient HTTP responses and throws UpstreamHttpError
  on non-ok, which would convert verbatim upstream error bodies into proxy
  502s.
- server.ts: main forward hop now uses it; each transparent replay logs a
  warn line with kind/delay/attempt.
- tests: new tests/main-path-transport-retry.test.ts (unit: refused/reset/DNS
  recovery, budget exhaustion, backoff shape, max=1 legacy switch,
  abort-during-backoff; server-level: reset mid-round -> one 200, persistent
  failure -> 502 after exactly 3 attempts, 4xx verbatim passthrough).
- e2e-relay-5xx-selfheal / issue1493-arm-outbound-payload pin
  BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX=1: they assert the single-attempt failure shape.
- CONFIGURATION.md/.zh-CN: document the extended scope of the two knobs.

Behavior change (old -> new): main model-request transport failures of
fail-fast kinds previously failed the round after 1 attempt; now up to 3
attempts total (default) with 1500ms->3000ms backoff before surfacing the
same 502. BILI_REPLAY_RETRY_MAX=1 restores the old behavior exactly. No new
config surface; HTTP-level responses are never retried on this path.
